racecards.race_name: Slater Menswear Handicap Hurdle

runners.comment: Has a long absence to overcome and a hefty weight for his handicap debut
runners.spotlight: Point and dual bumper winner who was a shade of odds-on when leading late on in a big-field maiden at Warwick in November 2024 (good to soft; won on soft); has a long absence to overcome and a hefty weight for his handicap debut, but trainer has spoken well of him.

quotes.race: Thank You Wetherby Groundstaff #Groundsweek Open NH Flat Race (Cat 1 Elimination) (Qualifier) (GBB)
quotes.quote: Castle Ivers is a lovely horse. We'll think about Aintree and Ayr for him but he's more a horse for next season - Olly Murphy, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: A point-to-point winner who won two bumpers last season but was over the top when he went to Aintree in April. He'll start off in a maiden hurdle next month and is one of my brighter novice hurdling prospects. 24-10-24

runners.comment: In form but does look vulnerable off this high a mark in this strong a race
runners.spotlight: Versatile trip-wise as his recent run of solid form has been from 1m7f to 3m; should give his running but does look vulnerable off this high a mark in this strong a race.

runners.comment: Debut winner for this yard and his Fred Winter run was better that it looks on paper
runners.spotlight: 1m2f French Flat winner who did well for former Irish connections, in victory and defeat over hurdles; even better when winning comfortably on his stable debut at Sandown (soft) and it was only three days later he finished well held under a penalty (same mark here) in the Fred Winter, though that run was better than it looks on paper; this is his first handicap against older opposition and he's very much in the mix.

quotes.race: Betfair Racing Podcasts Juvenile Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: The Fred Winter is where Bibe Mus is going to run. His mark of 122 is usually good enough to get in, but we had to run again to get the penalty. He'll go as long as he's all right. It'll take a little bit out of him, but he's a tough horse. I've liked what I've seen from him. He's filled out, strengthened up and taken well to our system. He wings up over our hill and he's a bonny, proper horse. Next season he'll be a fun horse for races like the Imperial Cup - Paul Nicholls, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's only just arrived at the yard after Colm Donlon bought him from Simon Munir and Isaac Souede. He's got some good form after finishing second in a Listed race at Aintree, then second again at Punchestown recently and we're going to take him to the Fred Winter. 15-02-26

runners.owner: A H B Hodge & Mrs H Cheape
runners.comment: Raced too freely in a Grade 2 last time; the ability is there should the hood help
runners.spotlight: Kelso novice winner in October (2m, good; effective on soft) and continued to run well until racing too freely in a Grade 2 at Kelso last time out; well held in a bumper when he tried a hood once before but this aid is worth another go.

quotes.race: Justin & Susan Greig Novices' Hurdle (Go North Night Nurse Series Qualifier) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Caballo De Guerra has loads of scope and won well. He's a bit keen, but I think the jumping will settle him down. The two in behind were pleasing, we know the winner is a good horse - Lucinda Russell, joint-trainer.

stable_tour.quote: We've always liked him. He was a bit keen in his races and it turned into a bit of a sprint at Cheltenham last Saturday, which didn't suit. He jumped great, however, and came out of it with plenty of credit. He still looks like an exciting prospect and could end up in quite a nice handicap. 29-10-25

runners.comment: Up 8lb for winning a weaker race last time but he does seem on an upward curve
runners.spotlight: Lightly raced 7yo who is 2-2 since sent into handicaps, both wins over 1m7f on good to soft ground at Musselburgh; an 8lb rise seems harsh enough for last time, for all that he won readily, and this a lot deeper; still respected with him on an upward curve.

stable_tour.quote: He has won his last two races, both at Musselburgh. He's going to go back there for the Go North final on March 20. He's a very nice horse who's going the right way. He's got a good engine, but a funny pedigree - a Flat pedigree. We're just going to tidy up his jumping a bit to make it a bit slicker, but I'm looking forward to the final with him. 12-02-26

runners.comment: Below par in two of his three races this season but he's on his last winning mark
runners.spotlight: Won a Class 3 handicap at Haydock last season off this mark so wouldn't be too dismissive about his chances despite failing to reach anything like the same level in two of his three races this campaign.

quotes.race: Sky Bet Acca Freeze Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: Bertie's Ballet is our pride and joy and we're delighted. He was a little lacking in confidence, but we've built that up and today he had to stand up and be counted - Dianne Sayer, trainer.

quotes.race: Betfred TV EBF 'National Hunt' Novices' Hurdle (Qualifier) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: He's such a professional. We've loved Bertie's Ballet since the day he came. He's enjoying his job and he'll keep learning and growing. The owners won the EBF Final at Sandown with Sam's Gunner and it will be nice to head down that road again - Dianne Sayer, trainer.

runners.comment: Highly tried since winning his 3yo hurdle; new headgear for this handicap debut
runners.spotlight: On his first two runs for this yard he won a 1m3f handicap on heavy and a 3yo hurdle on good to yielding; not so good since, albeit at Grade 2 and Listed level; might yet do better again and canny Irish trainer fits two new forms of headgear for this handicap debut; interesting.

stable_tour.quote: He's a nice horse with a huge pedigree and won well at Punchestown last month. He jumps really well - he loves jumping. The plan is to go to the Cheltenham November meeting for the juvenile hurdle. 04-11-25

runners.comment: Made all at Warwick; it's tougher dominating around here and he's 6lb higher
runners.spotlight: Maiden winner in Ireland and later placed in handicaps over fences; only his second run for this yard when dropped back to 2m in this new headgear combination at Warwick (good to soft) and he made pretty much every yard; it will be tougher dominating this stronger field on this more galloping track, and he's 6lb higher.

quotes.race: Bet Smarter With Oddschecker Conditional Jockeys' Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: After the last day we thought we might try Newton Rambler over this trip and make good use of him and we got it spot on. I should've sat quiet on him at the second-last and asked him for a long stride when I didn't need, but the horse knows what he's doing - Oakley Brown, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

runners.comment: Confidently ridden when second here last time; looks capable of better again
runners.spotlight: Beat Lance Les Des and Bertie's Ballet off 4lb lower at Kelso in February (2m, heavy) and he was confidently ridden out the back when second over C&D last time (soft), where a late mistake didn't help; strong suspicion that he more to offer and the yard, also represented by Caballo De Guerra, won this with a novice two years ago.

quotes.race: Racing TV Club Day Handicap Hurdle (Challenger Two Mile Hurdle Series Qualifier)
quotes.quote: We felt Triple Crown Ted ran too free at Ayr last time and Derek understood we needed to change tactics and sit him in to try to get him to switch off. We've always thought a lot of him - Peter Scudamore, assistant trainer.

runners.owner: Mrs David Coltman & Mrs J Douglas Miller
runners.comment: Exposed 10yo whose powers would appear to be on the wane
runners.spotlight: Exposed 10yo whose powers would appear to be on the wane judged on this season's performances; opposable.

stable_tour.quote: He's ready to go. I'll probably wait until December 8 or 9 at Kelso, where he's run his best races. We want to go over 2m as there's an ideal race for him on that card. Or we could run him beforehand, possibly at Haydock this week over 2m3f or in a valuable 2m handicap at Doncaster at the beginning of December. The question is whether I run him soon out of impatience, but equally he goes well fresh, so I might just wait. We want to be aiming him at the high-level 2m handicap hurdles. I'd love to take him back to the Morebattle, which he was second in last year. He was well beaten in the Scottish Champion Hurdle but actually ran well in that race. 21-11-24

runners.breeder: E A R L De Faydeau
runners.comment: Maiden winner last time; progressive and quite likely on fair terms with the handicapper
runners.spotlight: Closely matched with Triple Crown Ted on February's Kelso clash and this 7yo was good value for his win back in a maiden here last time on soft ground; progressive and quite likely on fair terms with the handicapper.

runners.owner: A Sinclair, I Jardine & V Renwick
runners.comment: Consistent but not progressive; fifth in this last year off the very same mark
runners.spotlight: Sole success in 17 runs over hurdles came at Perth last summer (2m, good); he's consistent but not progressive and was a well-held fifth in this last year off the very same mark.

stable_tour.quote: He's got loads of ability but is a tricky customer. He reached a pretty high level on the Flat and he's enjoying hurdles. He won in decisive fashion at Perth in July and then didn't run too badly back there last time. He might be best running fresh, though. We might consider chasing and somewhere like Musselburgh, where the fences are a bit smaller, could suit him. 10-09-25

runners.comment: Over fences for his last three races and has been good and bad; others preferred
runners.spotlight: All three wins have been here, a hurdle and two chases; over fences for his last three races and has been good and bad; others preferred.

stable_tour.quote: He's done quite well. He was bought as a pointer for my son Ben, but he won a 2m handicap hurdle at Ayr in March and was then third at the Scottish National meeting. He'll go to Perth on Thursday and then go chasing in the autumn. 16-05-24

runners.comment: Dropping back to 2m could work but this still commands a career best and by some way
runners.spotlight: Lightly raced maiden who took too strong a hold when a fading fourth on handicap debut at Musselburgh four weeks ago (good to soft); dropping back to 2m from 2m4f could work but this still commands a career best and by some way.

runners.comment: Returning to slower ground may help but unlikely that he's on that great a mark
runners.spotlight: Flat background; mildly progressive when first then second in two 4yo hurdles but he ran miserably switched to handicaps at Sedgefield where his jumping didn't stand the test; returning to slower ground may help but unlikely that he's on that great a mark.

racecards.verdict: Bibe Mus and Secret Force are shortlisted but this race could be ideal for the novice TRIPLE CROWN TED who travels strongly.
racecards.betting_forecast: 7/2 Secret Force, 9/2 Magna Victor, 6/1 Castle Ivers,  Bibe Mus, 8/1 Newtown Rambler,  Lance Les Des, 9/1 Triple Crown Ted, 10/1 The Gray Ghost, 20/1 Caballo De Guerra,  Bertie's Ballet,  Ravenscraig Castle,  Belaya River, 33/1 Ginger Mail,  Dance Thief,  Tuppence

racecards.race_name: Irish Thoroughbred Marketing Novices' Limited Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners.comment: He's struggled on his last two runs but perhaps wind op/cheekpieces will make a difference
runners.spotlight: Two-time novice hurdle winner who ran well in defeat this term on two of his first three chase starts (1m7f/2m, soft/good) and is on a handy mark on that form; he's struggled on his last two runs and has something to prove but perhaps the wind op and first-time cheekpieces will make a difference.

quotes.race: Join Racing TV Today Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Pleasington has been a challenge as he's had three runs now in three years but he's got lots of ability. We've always liked him but he's been a bit of a slow burner shall we say - Olly Murphy, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He could be a nice novice chaser as he jumps a fence well. He loves soft conditions, so we'll start him off in a novice chase as soon as there's some ease in the ground. 23-10-25

runners.comment: Front-runner; under pressure when falling last time but 3-3 in handicap chases previously
runners.spotlight: Front-runner; made mistakes and was under pressure when falling three out at Haydock (2m4f, soft) two months ago; however, he was 3-3 in handicap chases (1m7f-2m4f, soft/good to soft) previously and this very lightly raced 7yo may still have more to offer.

quotes.race: Sky Bet Extra Places Handicap Chase (Go North Monet's Garden Series Qualifier) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: There was a bit of discussion about the trip but if Throatlash was ever going to get two and a half, it was round here. Nobody is saying he's a star, he's just a lovely horse with a great attitude who jumps like a buck. He's the biggest horse I've ever had. He's enormous, a full 18 hands and a bit more. He's a novice all season so we'll step him up quietly. - Donald McCain, trainer.

quotes.race: William Hill Extra Places With B.O.G Novices' Limited Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Throatlash is such a big horse that I was moaning a bit because the fences were missing as I thought it was our one chance of winning. He was so good at Wetherby as well and this was great -  Donald McCain, trainer.

quotes.race: Watch Racing TV In HD Novices' Handicap Chase (Go North Forgive 'N Forget Series Qual') (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Throatlash is probably the biggest horse I've ever trained. Ballabriggs was 17.1 or 17.2 and this lad's enormous. I think a lot of people didn't buy him because he was so big. But he's the kindest you've ever seen and he jumps like a buck. He should improve for his first run of the season as well - Donald McCain, trainer.

runners.breeder: S C E A Haras Du Ma & Mr Marc Dumont
runners.comment: In good form at Chepstow on last two starts; optimism he'll be fine back down in trip
runners.spotlight: Beaten on first seven chase starts but showed improved form to win comfortably at Chepstow (2m3f, soft) in February and he bumped into a progressive winner there (2m3f, soft) last month, when clear of the third; there can be optimism that he will be fine back down in trip and he's respected.

quotes.race: Join The Vickers.Bet Free Bet Club Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Risk De Pluie is a very relaxed individual and he doesn't have to make the running. I wouldn't even be afraid to drop him to two miles, because two miles on soft ground would be fine. All options are open with him, so he'll come on for the run and we're very excited about him - Ben Clarke, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's probably the nicest horse I train, although ratings don't suggest that. He has decent form from his novice hurdles and is very smart. There's a piece of the jigsaw missing at the moment and we're not quite sure what it is. We'll have a go at a couple of nice prizes and if he wins, great, and if he doesn't he's still a novice for next season. Maybe he wants better ground or 3m. We'll laugh at his mark in time. He's better than 114. 12-03-25

runners.comment: 2-2 over fences and something to spare each time; may well have more left in the tank
runners.spotlight: Built upon his hurdling promise to win on chase/seasonal debut at Newcastle (2m, heavy) in January and he followed up there (2m, good to soft) in February; climbing the weights but this unexposed 7yo had something to spare for both wins and may well have more left in the tank.

quotes.race: Jimmy Hunter 60th Birthday Celebration Novices' Handicap Chase (Qualifier) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: He's been good. We thought The Grafter would improve for a fence, he's got the size and he's always jumped hurdles well - Sam England, trainer.

quotes.race: High Gosforth Park Golf Club Novices' Handicap Chase (Go North Forgive 'N Forget Qualifier) (GBB)
quotes.quote: My arm has been plated and all the rest of it; I had my fair time off. The guys at Jack Berry House did a brilliant job getting me back. I was worried about whether I'd be able to get a hold of The Grafter but he schooled well at home and he took a tug after the first few, so I let him go. I'm a little ring-rusty but I wanted to do something rather than nothing over the last. - Jonathan England, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

stable_tour.quote: He's just come back into work after holidaying with his owners, who gave him kissing-spine surgery in the summer. He's had a long and slow rehabilitation, so he probably won't be out until after January, but he ran really well over hurdles last season and was unlucky not to win. He was a big, immature horse who was learning all the time and should improve over fences. When he learns to settle, he might get further than 2m. 29-10-25

runners.comment: Disappointing on last 2 runs but good start to chasing career previously; may bounce back
runners.spotlight: Won his first two chase starts in January (2m, good/good to soft) under Jonjo O'Neill, who is back on board today; disappointing at Newbury on his last two outings but the first was a tough assignment over 2m4f and he jumped badly last time; it wouldn't be a surprise to see him bounce back.

quotes.race: Sky Bet, For The Fans Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Koukeo is going the right way and did everything right. They went a good gallop and he saw out the race well and was tough. When he got on better ground up the straight, he jumped better - Jonjo O'Neill, joint-trainer.

stable_tour.quote: It was probably all a bit too much for him going over to Punchestown for his first outing in April, but he'd shown some nice pieces of work before finishing second at Chepstow last month. He'll be going over hurdles now and we're keen to get some experience into him. He could be a nice stayer down the line. 06-11-24

runners.comment: Arrives on a five-timer and latest 7lb rise may not stop this thriving 8yo
runners.spotlight: Prominent racer who made it 4-4 for 2026 (1m7f-2m4f, good to soft/good) at Carlisle last month; won by 3l last time and a 7lb rise may not stop this thriving 8yo, provided the forecast soft ground isn't an issue.

quotes.race: Mark Nield Wealth Management Go North One Man Series Final Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: What a star Marty McFly is. His jumping has got better and better and he probably jumped even better again today. He didn't miss a beat. Danny gave him a great ride because it's not easy when something goes off like that - Sandy Thomson, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: We were really disappointed with him at Ayr the other day and maybe it was the desperate ground. We haven't had him that long and are just finding out about him. He'll make a nice novice chaser next season. 22-01-25

runners.comment: Hard to fancy on chasing evidence but this Irish raider is well treated on his hurdle form
runners.spotlight: Hard to fancy on the evidence of his four runs over fences this year; however, he's well handicapped on last summer's hurdle form and he's from a respected Irish stable; one to watch in the betting.

quotes.race: Join Racing TV With A Free Trial Now Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: I was kind of happy enough that they had gone a good gallop early on and I was happy enough to give them a little bit of rope heading down the back straight to get a little breather in and I finished off well because of that. Stuntman Steve's form is consistent, I had only ridden him once beforehand but it was over a longer trip and he rides like he wants a little bit further but then I don't know if he stays it so he is a little bit in between. A strongly run race probably suits him - Sean Flanagan, jockey.

quotes.race: Connolly's RED MILLS Irish EBF Auction Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: The final hurdle was the winning of the race for Stuntman Steve and thankfully he came up for me. We have him six weeks and while he hadn't been away, we thought he was a nice horse so thought he'd go close - Keith Donoghue, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: He had more letters than numbers in his point-to-point form but he's a grand horse. He won at Ballingarry in May and then made a winning start for us in a maiden hurdle at Clonmel last week when the front two pulled 17 lengths clear. I'm not sure where we go from here but he's qualified for the auction final at Punchestown. I suppose a rated novice could be next for him. 12-11-24

He's a grand horse who won his maiden hurdle at Clonmel last week and the front two pulled 17 lengths clear. He's qualified for the auction final at Punchestown and I suppose a rated novice could be next. 13-11-24

runners.comment: Likes it here & has won twice this term but needs to be better than ever back up in grade
runners.spotlight: Made it two wins for the season when scoring over C&D (soft) in January and bounced back from lesser run here when 1l second of five over C&D (soft) last month; could give another good account but he needs to be better than ever back up in grade if he's to win today.

quotes.race: Weatherbys Scientific Handicap Hurdle (Go North Sea Pigeon Series Qualifier)
quotes.quote: I'm really happy with Ballyfort. Last time his head came up and he didn't quite go through with it, but he did this time, so that's brilliant - Nick Alexander, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He was bought in May from the Irish point-to-point field, where he showed solid form. He was an eyecatching fifth on her debut in a novice hurdle at Ayr and there should be loads more to come from him. He should have a bright future. 22-11-23

runners.comment: Two wins at Sedgefield this season but 8lb wrong today and the cheekpieces are left off
runners.spotlight: Progressive in cheekpieces, winning at Sedgefield in November (2m1f, soft; hurdles) and March (2m, good; fences); should appreciate going back left-handed after being soundly beaten at Carlisle last time but he's 8lb out of the handicap today and the cheekpieces are left off.

stable_tour.quote: A giant of a horse, he's 17.3 hands and one of the biggest I've ever had. He had a lovely run last time when third at Wetherby. He's only five and is a big baby. You won't see the best of him until he goes over fences. He'll run at Christmas time and it could be in a chase. 11-12-24

racecards.verdict: Having impressed when winning at Newcastle on his first two chase starts, THE GRAFTER can maintain his unbeaten record over fences.
racecards.betting_forecast: 100/30 The Grafter, 4/1 Marty McFly, 11/2 Throatlash, 6/1 Risk De Pluie, 13/2 Pleasington,  Stuntman Steve, 11/1 Koukeo, 12/1 Ballyfort, 20/1 Tanking Along

racecards.race_name: Abbott Risk Consulting Ltd Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Below par at Christmas but had a break and can go well if back on song
runners.spotlight: 0-3 in bumpers and 0-4 over hurdles, but has some respectable form and wasn't himself at Sedgefield last time when held at his point of departure; had a break since Christmas and can go well if back on song.

runners.comment: Has been weakening over longer trips in previous maidens; had a wind operation
runners.spotlight: Has been running well for a long way before weakening in maidens over 2m3f and 2m5f (tongue tied in final run); could have a better run in him after wind surgery and he's of definite interest.

runners.comment: 2m4f perhaps too far last time; previous Down Royal fourth over 2m1f was a good effort
runners.spotlight: A good run to be fourth on yielding ground in a 2m1f maiden at Down Royal in December and when below that level here two months ago he was sent over 2m4f (on soft); connections presumably not fazed by today's ground and, returned to shorter, he shouldn't be far away.

runners.breeder: S C E A Ste Ent Etienne Et Gregoire Lee
runners.comment: By some way it was his best performance yet when second to odds-on winner here last time
runners.spotlight: By some way it was his best performance yet when the only one to give the odds-on winner a race over C&D (soft) in late March; may need to take another step forward here but that's quite feasible.

runners.breeder: S C E A Ecurie Haras De La Rousseliere
runners.owner: Mrs Diana L Whateley, McNeill & Stone Families
runners.comment: Two encouraging runs in bumpers, the latest after a long absence; hurdle debut
runners.spotlight: Bought for £60,000 after finishing an 11l second to the classy Mydaddypaddy in a Huntingdon bumper last March; only returned this February when beaten a short-head here by a Russell/Scudamore horse with potential; now goes over hurdles.

runners.comment: Close second in point bumper but it's been a quiet start under rules
runners.spotlight: Close second in point bumper but it's been a quiet start under rules with 286 days separating heavy defeats in a bumper and novice hurdle.

stable_tour.quote: He's a full-brother to Magna Victor and I'm looking forward to him coming out soon. He's had just one run in the point-to-point bumper at Aintree in May. He was a bit disappointing then but I'm hopeful there's more to come from him. 12-02-26

runners.comment: No worthwhile form in bumpers or over hurdles and she can be readily dismissed
runners.spotlight: No worthwhile form in bumpers or over hurdles and she can be readily dismissed.

runners.comment: 0-6 over hurdles; gets all the allowances as a 4yo filly but others have greater upside
runners.spotlight: Dual Flat winner; 0-6 over hurdles and the worst of those runs was the latest in a handicap at Carlisle; gets all the allowances as a 4yo filly but others probably have greater upside even if she is back to something like her best.

racecards.verdict: Preference is for DROPEMATTHESTATION who has been running well only to fade over longer distances and he's also had a wind operation.
racecards.betting_forecast: 7/4 Lirion, 7/2 Dropematthestation, 9/2 Green Angel, 5/1 Bohemond Antioch, 6/1 Linalene, 12/1 Penn Avenue, 25/1 Magna Patch, 200/1 Culzean

racecards.race_name: Hillhouse Quarry Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Front-runner who was second at Newbury last month and can make another bold bid
runners.spotlight: Front-runner; won two in a row last autumn (2m3f/2m4f, good to soft) and back to form when second under Jay Tidball at Newbury (2m4f, good to soft) last month; effective on soft earlier in career; can make another bold bid.

stable_tour.quote: He was unfortunate on New Year's Day ? he's a good jumper but just made a mistake. He prefers quicker ground and may run in the Greatwood Gold Cup at Newbury in a couple of weeks, so he's only a possible for the festival. He'd have to go and win very well there to justify his entry in the Ryanair. 15-02-26

He won his point-to-point last December in the style of a nice horse and I was confident before his Hereford bumper last spring. He won nicely by 12 lengths and followed up under a penalty at Haydock on his only other start. That was a good performance and augurs well for this term. He has schooled beautifully, and I am looking at starting him back at Fakenham on Friday, ground permitting. I rate him as an exciting prospect and the plan is to start small before stepping up in grade. 13-10-22

runners.comment: Won at Kempton in February and mistakes didn't help when soundly beaten there last time
runners.spotlight: Soundly beaten fourth at Kempton (2m4f, good) last month but mistakes didn't help; won there (2m4f, good to soft) two starts ago and he can be in the mix if cutting out the errors; probably okay on soft ground.

quotes.race: Sidney Banks Memorial Novices' Hurdle (Listed Race) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We knew if Califet En Vol was in the argument two out that he would come home strongly and he's basically outstayed them. We'd rather this race be two miles and five than just short of two and a half but he overcame it and was strong through the finish. I don't think Cheltenham is the right way to go with him this year as he's still just a baby and there is a three-mile novice at Aintree and beyond that a race at Ayr, although we would have to mind him if we went there as he likes to get his toe in. We won this race with Shishkin a few years ago and hopefully this horse can be in the same sentence as him down the line - Nicky Henderson, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's done really well and has grown into a fine, big chasing type. He won the Sidney Banks at Huntingdon in February, which is no mean feat. He was running a seriously good race at Aintree in the Grade 1 [Sefton Novices' Hurdle over three miles], but he made a right mess at the second-last and went backwards. He came with an injury on his off-fore and I thought we were in big trouble. He was very sore, but he's fine now and he'll go chasing. 21-10-25

runners.comment: Has something to prove but major player if tapping back into last season's promise
runners.spotlight: Prone to making a bad blunder and arrives with something to prove following heavy defeats on his last two starts; however, he hasn't been devoid of promise this season and he'll be a major player if tapping back into the promise shown when romping to victory at last season's Cheltenham Festival.

quotes.race: Ultima Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We knew that if Myretown jumped round, he was phenomenally well-handicapped; I just didn't know if he was going to be man enough, and it's very exciting that he is. He's a novice horse, his jumping has been a bit hit and miss, he turned upside down at Windsor, but since then we ran him at Kelso and he's got his confidence back. He's a bit different to Corach Rambler - he jumps so exuberantly. Corach is just a different sort of horse, but this is a phenomenal horse - Lucinda Russell, trainer.

quotes.race: Every Horse, Every Race, At timeform.com Novices' Limited Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Myretown was much more grown up today and that opens options up for us. I'd like to keep Derek [Fox] on him so we wouldn't go for the Kim Muir or anything and we'll look at a novice chase at Uttoxeter after Cheltenham - Lucinda Russell, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He flew the flag for us last season by winning at Cheltenham. He'll start off in the Coral Gold Cup, but he'll have a couple of racecourse gallops before Newbury. He's got to take another step forward, but he's got the profile to do so. He couldn't have been any more impressive in the Ultima, albeit off a mark that in a normal year wouldn't have got him into the race. He's got a long way to go and perhaps Grand Nationals are more realistic than Gold Cups, but he's very lightly raced. With Corach Rambler, the Ultima was a good Grand National trial and that's in the back of our minds. 29-10-25

runners.comment: Won a quality handicap at Cheltenham in January and a 5lb rise isn't harsh
runners.spotlight: Can make mistakes but he was runner-up twice in a row prior to winning a quality handicap at Cheltenham (2m4f, soft) in January, when clear with subsequent Ultima runner-up Jagwar; a 5lb rise for that career-best performance isn't harsh and he's entitled to respect.

quotes.race: Betfair Exchange Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Donnacha has never been out of the frame and his form over hurdles here is top-class. It's what racing's all about. It's absolutely priceless. The owners have just got the one horse, they've had him since he was a three-year-old and they've been very patient. They deserve everything they get - Nigel Hawke, trainer.

quotes.race: Text Fitzdares On 07492 882213 Novices' Limited Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Donnacha is improving all the time and is a great jumper. There's a possibility of that novice handicap chase at Cheltenham, but we'll see what the handicapper does or there's Sandown [March 8], we could go two and a half miles there. Because it's a new race, no one's got a guide of where the bottom line is, but if we get into it on a realistic mark it would have to be looked at for sure - Nigel Hawke, trainer.

quotes.race: Michael Costello Memorial Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: His form at Cheltenham is solid and it was good to get his head in front. Donnacha probably wasn't in love with that soft ground but he's a work in progress and improving all the time. He's in the Betfair Hurdle and we'll see how he comes out of this. The County Hurdle or Martin Pipe at Cheltenham could be other options - Nigel Hawke, trainer.

runners.comment: On a reduced mark and could be in the shake-up back down in trip and in grade
runners.spotlight: 9yo who hasn't been at his best this season but there have been signs of spark and he failed to stay 3m2f when well beaten at the Cheltenham Festival last time; continues to drop down the weights and could be in the shake-up back down in trip and in grade.

quotes.race: Paddy Power Gold Cup Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Il Ridoto will come back for the December Gold Cup as he loves it here. The ground was perfect for him today. He's not a Grade One horse, he's a good handicapper and has won his big race. He had had a run at Chepstow, a month's work at home and had a nice light weight. He deserved it today - Paul Nicholls, trainer.

quotes.race: Paddy Power Cheltenham Countdown Podcast Handicap Chase (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I thought El Ridoto had a big chance of winning here the last day but he sort of ducked in left handed and fell through the last and that sort of cost him any chance really. I think a few were doubting about whether he wanted a flat track and whether he truly stayed. I thought he was kidding us a little bit as he was coming out of his races so well and the cheekpieces have focused his mind today. He travelled and jumped brilliantly and had a great ride so it's superb - Paul Nicholls, trainer.

quotes.race: Watch Racing Free Online At Ladbrokes Handicap Chase (For The Jim Joel Memorial Trophy) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: That was a good performance from Il Ridoto and it was a long-term plan as Paul had won this race with another four-year-old, Ulck Du Lin, in 2012. He was a bit flat out the first mile - I think they went quite hard - and the race became about stamina, and he jumped well. We wouldn't be in a mad rush to go further because of his age, but I think he'll end up over a trip. He's entered at Sandown on Friday, but I don't think Paul will be in a hurry with him - Harry Derham, assistant trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He always comes on for his first run and ran an excellent trial for the Paddy Power Gold Cup when runner-up at Chepstow a few weeks ago. What's more, he has worked in eye-catching style since then, so I see no reason why he won't run a mighty race when going for a repeat in the big race at Cheltenham this month. Last season's victory, which meant his form figures in the race now stand at 431, was thoroughly deserved as it had taken an age for his rating to come down. An 8lb hike for that success meant it was game over as far as he was concerned and he's been well held in five outings since. But he's slipped back down the weights again and he'll be just 1lb higher than 12 months ago in the Paddy Power. He's more effective in the autumn than the spring and I'm confident he'll go to Cheltenham spot on. 04-11-25

runners.comment: Well beaten at Cheltenham last month but that may not be his track; in good heart before
runners.spotlight: Well beaten in the Plate last month but Cheltenham may not be his track; comfortably made all in small field at Leicester (2m6f, good to soft) in January and led into the straight at Ascot (3m, good to soft) in February, only to weaken; also effective on soft; could be involved.

quotes.race: Coral Racing Club Join For Free Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: Kielan has given Jipcot a lovely ride. He got him settled and was jumping lovely, so it's great to see it work out for everyone. The Megsons have been very patient with the horse and hopefully he can keep improving. He has plenty of quirks, so I don't think we'll ever stop learning about him, as he definitely has ideas of his own - AJ O'Neill, joint-trainer.

quotes.race: Richard Howard Memorial Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: Jipcot is a bit of a hothead to train and it's quite obvious the way to ride him is with a tongue-tie and a hood. He'll have an entry now for next weekend in the Imperial Cup. I think he'll actually be good for coming out again quickly. I always wanted to run him in the Imperial Cup but he wouldn't have got in off his handicap mark [of 117]. With a 7lb penalty he will and this was our last chance - Ben Pauling, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He won a handicap hurdle at Newbury last December, and that was when you saw the real Jipcot. He just needs things to fall right for him and we're going to go chasing this term. He's already got some experience over fences and we'd like to go for something like the Sir Peter O'Sullevan Memorial Handicap Chase at the Coral Gold Cup meeting. There's no doubt he has the ability, but he probably needs a fast-run race to bring out the best in him. 18-11-25

runners.comment: Has had wind surgery and top trainer has won five of the last eight runnings of this race
runners.spotlight: He hasn't quite been at the top of his game on his last two starts; however, he's had wind surgery since and is certainly of interest on his two third-place finishes at Cheltenham in the autumn (3m1f/2m4f, good/soft); top trainer has won five of the last eight runnings of this race.

quotes.race: Paddy Power Gold Cup Handicap Chase (In Memory Of Edward O'Grady) (Premier Handicap) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I said to Hoe Joly Smoke's owners I have to run this horse on the form he'd be showing us at home. He'd had a prep run and the obvious thing to do was drop back in drip - Dan Skelton, trainer.

quotes.race: Best Odds On The Betfair Exchange Handicap Chase (Challenger Staying Chase Series Qual') (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Harry [Skelton] got off Hoe Joly Smoke immediately and said the Scottish National, but I just wouldn't want to go to Ayr and not run well, whereas we've got two weeks and we can come here to a track we know suits him. He's improving and everything about the bet365 will suit him. I like coming back to the scene of victories and obviously he likes this track. He's still a novice over hurdles, so next year we might have one run over hurdles, then find the nicest chase we can - Dan Skelton, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He ran really well on his reappearance in a 3m1f handicap chase at Cheltenham. He travelled into it like he was going to win and I can't say he blew up because we'd done a good bit with him at home, so I have to think he just didn't stay. We'll drop him back in trip next time and I think there could be a good prize heading his way. 10-11-25

runners.comment: 11 visits to Ayr have yielded five wins and this is his time of year; could go well
runners.spotlight: Won over C&D (soft) in February before respectable sixth of 17 in veterans' final at Haydock (2m4f, good) a fortnight ago; 11 visits to Ayr have yielded five wins and this is his time of year; could go well.

quotes.race: Every Race Live On Racing TV Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I was absolutely delighted with his performance. At his age, carrying that weight and on that ground, I thought Dubai Days was pretty brave. Horses like him are hard to come by. He keeps turning up time and time again. That [the Middle Distance Veterans' Chase Final at Haydock] would be the obvious race to run him in. It's about five weeks away, so hopefully, all being well, we'll head there - Nick Alexander,  trainer.

quotes.race: Unibet Middle Distance Chase Series Veterans' Handicap Chase (Series Qualifier)
quotes.quote: Dubai Days usually takes a couple of runs to show his best so to do that first time out is good. He had a little niggle in the autumn so we thought we'd get him as ready as we could at home because he can be very hard on himself. He'll be back here next month for the final now - Bruce Lynn, jockey.

quotes.race: Seko Logistics Scotland Novices' Limited Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Dubai Days is a lovely, consistent horse. He takes a chance with one or two but I think he'll be better as a second-season chaser. He's declared tomorrow but I don't think he'll run. There's a race back here for him in ten days but I may put him away - Nick Alexander, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He unfortunately had a setback but he's due to be back in training at the end of this month. He's always shown his best form in the spring anyway, so I'd be targeting similar races that he ran in last year. He's a veteran now too, so he can run in that 2m4f veterans' series. He certainly retains all of his ability. 21-11-24

prev_owners.owner: Mrs I Hodge & Hugh Hodge Ltd

runners.comment: Yet to get competitive this season but his three wins have all come at Ayr
runners.spotlight: Hasn't got competitive this term and beaten 18l when sixth of eight on stable debut at Kelso (2m1f, good to soft) in February; however, he shaped as though this step up in trip might be a good move and his three wins, including two over fences last January (2m, soft), have all come at Ayr.

quotes.race: Try Racing TV For Free Now Novices' Limited Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We thought the handicapper was harsh on Hombre De Guerra and he very nearly got him beaten! The only horse to beat him over fences is Caldwell Potter, which bodes well - Nick Alexander, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He was due to run at Ayr recently but we didn't want to run him on the good ground. He's ready to go chasing. He schools well and I'm looking forward to running him over fences. He's got the speed to run over 2m but ultimately he'll be a good 3m chaser. 21-11-24

racecards.verdict: This course and time of year brings out the best in DUBAI DAYS and he earns the vote ahead of Hombre De Guerra.
racecards.betting_forecast: 5/2 Donnacha, 7/2 Hoe Joly Smoke, 5/1 Califet En Vol, 15/2 Twinjets, 9/1 Il Ridoto,  Jipcot, 11/1 Myretown, 14/1 Hombre De Guerra, 16/1 Dubai Days

racecards.race_name: Coral Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners.owner: Mrs Jo Tracey, K Alexander, P&S Bryceland
runners.comment: Won at Warwick in February and when pulled up at Fontwell last time it was a Grade 2
runners.spotlight: Fourth in this last year (good to soft) and he comfortably made all at Warwick (2m5f, heavy) in February; pulled up at Fontwell 15 days later but that was a Grade 2; could make a bold bid back in a handicap.

quotes.race: Thank You White Horse Hinton Team Handicap Hurdle (Challenger Stayers Hurdle Series Qualifier)
quotes.quote: We thought we'd get a lead today and we also changed the bit that Phantomofthepoints ran in at Chepstow. Jack (Tudor) always thought he was doing enough on the run-in. David Pipe, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: It didn't work out for him in points but the form of his third in a Ballinrobe bumper has worked out well. He's a big, strong horse, a nice individual, and he'll start in a bumper somewhere before going over hurdles. 31-10-23

runners.comment: Improved form in this hood; contested Grade 3 last time; more needed back in a handicap
runners.spotlight: Improved form since this hood went on, comfortably defying a penalty in novice hurdle at Down Royal (2m1f, soft) in January before respectable efforts in 2m Listed/Grade 3 races; however, further improvement is needed back in a handicap and he has to prove his stamina.

quotes.race: Tayto Group Maiden Hurdle (Div I)
quotes.quote: Jony R was in good form coming here. To be fair to that horse, there is nothing flukey about it on the day. He hasn't been overly harshly-raced and he has really strengthened up over the summer. You definitely would see him over further and he did nothing wrong. He was a wee bit keen there, a wee bit fresh. I'll probably end up going across the water for a novice under a penalty rather than trying to step up in grade over here -Stuart Crawford, trainer.

runners.comment: Easily made all in this last year but he's struggled for form since chase win in December
runners.spotlight: Easily made all in this last year when 5lb higher and he's one to watch in the betting; however, he's struggled for form over fences/hurdles since winning a novice chase at Kelso in December.

quotes.race: Coral Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: The Four Sixes has an unbelievable constitution. He puts a lot into it and he probably won't run again this season - Olly Murphy, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's very tough and I'm keen to get him out over fences again. I think if he gets his jumping together he could be a really nice chaser from two and a half to three miles. He won at Ayr on good to soft ground, but I think he's better in softer conditions. He's got plenty of ability. 23-10-25

runners.comment: May well have completed hat-trick but for final-flight mistake at Newbury; strong claims
runners.spotlight: Improved in this tongue-tie in the winter, winning two handicaps (2m3f, soft), and he may well have completed a hat-trick but for a final-flight mistake in a novice at Newbury (2m4f, good to soft) four weeks ago; this smooth-travelling sort could have more left in the tank; strong claims.

quotes.race: bettingsites.co.uk New Betting Sites Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: Came From Nowhere picked up an injury after his second run over hurdles, so it's been a bit of a long road back. He's been running well without winning, so it's nice to bump into a race we can pick up. We might now look for a nice target for him in January - Jeremy Scott, trainer.

runners.comment: Promising novice this season and better than he showed in the Morebattle; not written off
runners.spotlight: Merely mid-division in the Morebattle at Kelso (2m, good to soft) in February having been backed into favouritism; however, he's been a promising novice this season and is capable of better than he showed last time; not written off up in trip.

runners.owner: J Fyffe And Mrs W Duffus
runners.comment: Made it 2-2 in this hood when winning on h'cap debut at Musselburgh; clearly progressive
runners.spotlight: Won maiden hurdle here (2m, soft) in January and back on the scoresheet in this hood on his last two starts, most recently on handicap debut at Musselburgh (2m4f, good to soft); this progressive 6yo did it nicely last time and a 5lb rise may not stop him this afternoon.

quotes.race: Heritage Portfolio Go North Night Nurse Series Final Novices' Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: To come and do that was great. You want good horses and Sanilam is a good horse. He had top weight and this wouldn't be his ideal track, he'll stay three miles in time. We need to get him to settle, he might have another season hurdling - Sandy Thomson, trainer.

quotes.race: Virgin Bet Supports Safe Gambling Novices' Hurdle (Go North Night Nurse Hurdle Series Qual') (GBB)
quotes.quote: Sanilam won over two miles at Ayr two starts ago but for a horse having his fourth run [over hurdles] the last day he did everything backwards. Sandy [Thomson] decided to put the hood on him and step him up in trip and it's had the desired effect. I probably got there sooner than ideal and he was a bit idle up the straight - Brian Hughes, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing

runners.comment: Ready win at Doncaster last month; could take 7lb rise in his stride; unproven on soft
runners.spotlight: Went back up in trip at Doncaster (2m5f, good to soft) last month on his second start since rejoining this yard and posted a ready win; this lightly raced 7yo could take a 7lb rise in his stride provided conditions are suitable (unproven on soft ground).

stable_tour.quote: A nice four-year-old who hasn't run and might go straight over hurdles. He's a big, galloping horse and, while he might win a bumper, I'd be inclined to let him learn his trade over hurdles as he's going along. 25-10-23

runners.comment: Won this in 2023 on sole previous course visit and has an each-way shout
runners.spotlight: 9yo who was tailed off at Kelso in February last time but that was the competitive Morebattle Hurdle over 2m; in good form over 2m4f at the end of last year, winning at Newcastle then second at Aintree; won this in 2023 on sole previous course visit and has an each-way shout back up in trip.

quotes.race: bet365 Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Serious Operator is improving, his jumping was perfect. We were a bit worried about the ground. His hurdling is outstanding and he'll go chasing next season - Lucinda Russell, trainer.

quotes.race: Bet Boost At bet365 Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: When Serious Operator gets his ground and gets everything sorted he's a heck of a horse. He couldn't get out of the heavy ground last time. Today he travelled and I probably got there too soon. I hope he's turned the corner now - Patrick Wadge, rider.

stable_tour.quote: He needs good ground and wasn't quite right last season. The rain came at the wrong time at Aintree, but it was a really encouraging run. We could see him coming good in a big-field handicap hurdle over two and a half miles. 29-10-25

He came to us from Daniel Murphy in Ireland having won two point-to-points. He won first time out for us under rules at Kelso and, after an unhappy run at Cheltenham in October, returned this month with a win over 2m4½f at Newcastle. He's not over-big but has a nice engine and stays exceedingly well. He's better on good to soft. After his Cheltenham run Tom [Scudamore] suggested he had breathing issues and he was subsequently operated on. He won after the operation but genuinely seems better than ever and we could head back to Cheltenham this weekend. He's a strong galloper and jumps well and long term I can't wait to see him novice chasing. 25-01-23

runners.owner: The Late John Hales And Miss L Hales
runners.comment: Two novice hurdle wins this season but pulled up on handicap debut at Haydock on Wednesday
runners.spotlight: Looked promising when winning maiden hurdle at Southwell (2m) in December and novice hurdle at Newcastle (2m1f, also good to soft) last month; however, pulled up on handicap debut at Haydock (2m5f, good) on Wednesday.

quotes.race: Download The At The Races App Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: It's game-changing to have a horse of his ability. We'll hopefully be looking at some nicer races in the future. He's a three-mile chaser in the making but Irandando Has has won in spite of the ground being quicker and the trip being shorter than ideal. We'll come up with a plan and see what the handicapper does, but we won't be in a rush with him and will give him plenty of time - Sam Allwood, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: All manner of niggling problems have prevented this big horse from getting to the track ever since he came to us from France two years ago. But I've seen enough to know there's an engine in there, so I hope the owners' patience will finally be rewarded when we get him to the track for a maiden hurdle in around six weeks' time. 04-11-24

runners.comment: Runner-up at Uttoxeter last month and winner followed up at Aintree last week; key player
runners.spotlight: Has done well since moving into handicaps, winning at Lingfield (2m7f, good to soft) in December and second of 14 at Uttoxeter (2m4f, soft) last month behind Wellington Arch, who followed up at Aintree last week; progressing nicely and he's a key player up 3lb for last time.

stable_tour.quote: His half-brother recently won a point-to-point by 24 lengths, which was nice. We went to Wincanton in November for an educational run but the favourite fell and he won easily, which wasn't ideal as we could have done with him being a novice for another season. He ended up coming out of it with a tibia fracture, so he's been on the easy list and won't run until the autumn. I rode him for the first time in three months last week. He's a very nice horse and will make a chaser, but he'll go handicap hurdling next season and then chasing the following year. He's a big baby but he'll improve masses for time. He can grow and mature now. 12-03-25

runners.comment: Maiden/novice wins at Kelso; did it easily last time and has potential off opening mark
runners.spotlight: Bumper winner who got off the mark over hurdles at the fourth attempt at Kelso (2m5f, soft) in November and was back on the scoresheet in a novice there (2m5f, good to soft) four weeks ago; did it easily last time and has potential off his opening mark.

runners.comment: Fourth of 14 at Kelso last time and the form looks solid; could again be thereabouts
runners.spotlight: Runner-up here (2m4f, soft) in November and suited by the step back up in trip when fourth of 14 at Kelso (2m5f, good to soft) four weeks ago, beaten just over 2l; that form looks solid; could again be thereabouts.

stable_tour.quote: He joined us from Pauline Robson. He was second in a handicap hurdle at Ayr last week, when he gave a lot of weight away to the winner. He did most things right and he'll go chasing now. He has won a bumper and over hurdles, and was then fifth in a Grade 2 hurdle at Kelso. Trips between 2m and 2m5f will suit for now, as will a bit of cut in the ground. 19-11-25

runners.comment: Continues to drop down weights but hasn't been shaping as though about to take advantage
runners.spotlight: This season hasn't been completely devoid of spark and he continues to drop down the weights, but he hasn't been shaping as though he's about to take advantage and his losing sequence is up to 11 races.

quotes.race: Trustatrader Novices' Hurdle (Grade 2) (Registered As The Hyde Novices' Hurdle) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Minella Missile is very laid back. I love a horse you can drop in and then they quicken, not many can get there in two strides but he can. Talk is talk and the men in March, they don't talk they just turn up. We're under no illusions and he's won his race. He's a half-brother to Monbeg Genius who I think is a very good horse and his future will be over fences somewhere down the line. For a staying novice hurdler he quickens - Evan Williams, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: I couldn't get him right after he won the Grade 2 contest at Cheltenham last year, so I just gave him time. I could have run him, but I was never 100 per cent happy, so we chose to be patient. I'm delighted with him now and he's ready to run. He's still not got much experience and it's difficult to find the right starting point, but he doesn't want it too deep and he'll have a few entries in the coming weeks. 25-11-24

This season has been a bit of a struggle for him, especially when you consider he won a Grade 2 novice hurdle at Cheltenham two years ago. He wore cheekpieces for the first time at Windsor on New Year's Day and that woke him up a bit, but he made a mistake two from home that meant he had to settle for fifth. He liked Windsor, so he'll go back there. 14-01-26

runners.breeder: Haras De Saint Voir Sca & Mr Joel Denis
runners.comment: In good form this season but suspicion he's vulnerable to stronger stayers at this trip
runners.spotlight: Easy win at Hexham (2m4f, good to soft) last October and he's continued to run well (soft/good to soft), finishing 11l fourth of 17 at Haydock (2m5f) in January on his last handicap start; not ruled out each-way although there's a suspicion he's vulnerable to stronger stayers at this trip.

stable_tour.quote: He won nicely at Hexham, but it's hard to judge that form as he handled the conditions that day better than anything. He's a young horse who still has plenty of potential. He's taken a while to settle in his races, but now he's open to any sort of improvement. 29-10-25

racecards.verdict: The progressive Came From Nowhere is a tempting option but preference is for A PERFECT DAY, who is also very much on the up.
