racecards.race_name: Get Home Safe With Thistle Cabs Handicap Hurdle

runners.comment: A return to form is needed but cheekpieces go on and he's in top hands; not written off
runners.spotlight: Below par on last three starts, most recently at Uttoxeter last month following wind surgery; however, he won off this mark on his reappearance at Aintree in November and first-time cheekpieces might give him a boost; in top hands and not written off.

quotes.race: William Hill Best Odds Guaranteed Novices' Limited Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I didn't think Hidden History would win, I thought he'd take a good blow. I think he'll still improve and softer ground will suit him as well. We'll perhaps give him six weeks, we won't rush him back. He'll probably stay any trip. The winner of the race last year went on to win the National Hunt Chase - maybe that's a predestined target - Dan Skelton, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: Won a 2m4f handicap hurdle for us last season and started out over fences with a win in a novice handicap chase over 3m1f on Saturday at Aintree, where the longer trip and the softer ground suited him. He jumped much better on the track than he had at home and I think he'll progress into the winter on that kind of ground and turn into a decent staying novice chaser.. 10-11-25

He did very well for us last season, winning on Midlands National day at Uttoxeter and then being a bit unlucky when just beaten at Perth. He's a proper mudlark and he's likely to be going chasing. I'd like to think there's still a bit of room in his mark. 22-10-25

runners.comment: Second to unexposed Skelton winner at Wetherby in February and has solid claims up 3lb
runners.spotlight: Admirably consistent in handicaps and finished second to an unexposed Skelton winner when upped in trip at Wetherby (3m, soft) in February, pulling clear of the third; solid claims up 3lb for last time.

stable_tour.quote: He bolted up in a bumper at Market Rasen in April and made a pleasing debut at Carlisle. He'll learn on the job and will definitely win his maiden and novice. 24-10-24

runners.owner: Mrs Jo Tracey, K Alexander & Russell

prev_owners.owner: Mrs Jo Tracey, K Alexander, P&S Bryceland

runners.comment: Hasn't shone over fences on last two runs but each-way claims on this season's hurdle form
runners.spotlight: Well beaten/pulled up over fences on his last two starts but he's produced positive performances over C&D (soft) on his two hurdle runs this season, finishing placed each time; each-way claims back over hurdles.

quotes.race: Karaoke At The Golf Inn Prestwick Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: Whistle Stop Tour is a really progressive 7yo and Derek [Fox] was really positive about him after his Kelso win. He has plenty of options open to him. There's the 3m6f novice handicap chase at Cheltenham, there's a nice race at Uttoxeter soon after or there's always the Scottish National back here. Our dream though would be the 2026 Grand National - Sean Tracey, joint-owner, talking to Racing TV.

stable_tour.quote: He ran some big races last year before everything went wrong in the Ultima when he was nearly brought down. We tried to rescue the season after that, but he's come back in great form. He looks so much stronger and you'd like to think he'd be a type who could build into a Scottish National horse. He stays very well. 29-10-25

runners.owner: Sir F Brooke & Sir R Pilkington
runners.comment: Soundly beaten in the EBF Final on handicap debut but this 6yo retains potential
runners.spotlight: Soundly beaten in mid-division on last month's handicap debut in the EBF Final at Sandown (2m4f, soft); however, that was a hot contest and this two-time novice hurdle winner (2m4f/2m5f, soft) retains potential, with the step up in trip a possible plus.

quotes.race: Sky Bet Club Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: For Draco Malfoy's first time over hurdles it was a nice performance. He is not the quickest, hence he didn't win a bumper, but he ran well in all his bumpers. When he arrived last year, I said he wasn't a hurdler yet. So, we gave him another year and played around in bumpers for a season. He will progress when he gets older, a bit like me! I don't think he will be in that league of Chianti Classico as he was a bit unique. He is in the same ownership as him though and they bought him after he won at Cheltenham. He has taken a while to come together this season as his blood has been wrong and we have just had to be patient and wait for him, but he has been worth waiting for. We will find another race over this trip under a penalty, but he has three miles written all over him - Kim Bailey, trainer.Once Draco Malfoy was beaten in his first bumper he was never going to win one of those but enjoyed it out there this today. He had excelled in his schooling and we came here confident -  Tom Bellamy, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: We're very pleased with him. We always liked him last year and when he didn't win his first bumper we thought it would be one of those years where he'd keep finishing placed, and he was quite immature. We've been delighted with him since he's come in this year, his schooling has been fantastic, and he did what we hoped at Huntingdon last time out. We'll try and find something small for him over the Christmas period under a penalty and then raise his sights after that. 24-12-25

runners.comment: Won on stable debut at Wetherby; tougher task today but unexposed over staying trips
runners.spotlight: Easily won a maiden hurdle at Carlisle (2m3f, soft) in December and he tapped back into that promise to win a handicap at Wetherby (3m, good) three weeks ago on his stable debut; beat just five rivals last time but this 6yo is unexposed over staying trips and could be a contender up 4lb.

runners.comment: He's struggled on his last two starts but won this last year; betting may be interesting
runners.spotlight: Tailed off (fences) and pulled up (hurdles) on his last two starts; a major turnaround is necessary but he runs off the same mark as when winning this race last year; not ruled out and the betting may be interesting.

runners.comment: Tough task when pulled up at Cheltenham Festival; ran well at this meeting last year
runners.spotlight: His chase form has been mixed this season but he faced a tough task from out of the handicap at the Cheltenham Festival (pulled up); runner-up at Kempton (2m5f) in November on last hurdle start and he was second over fences at this meeting 12 months ago (3m); might not be a forlorn hope today.

runners.comment: Hopes are pinned on the wind op and first-time tongue-tie prompting a transformation
runners.spotlight: 2-3 over hurdles in France; he's returned from a long absence this season and been well beaten in a chase and handicap hurdle; hopes are pinned on the wind op and first-time tongue-tie prompting a transformation.

stable_tour.quote: He'll go novice chasing and he's schooled very well over fences. He could start at the Coral Gold Cup meeting or the week after. I think he'll end up wanting two and a half miles this season but I might start him at two miles. I'm very excited by him - he's a proper horse. I was very keen to get him back at the David Maxwell dispersal sale as I put a lot of work into him last season. 19-11-25

runners.owner: Mr And Mrs J D Cotton
runners.comment: Ex-French 7yo; the form of his Newbury second has worked out well; firmly in calculations
runners.spotlight: Three-time French hurdle winner who was pulled up on his chase and stable debut in January but returned to form when second over hurdles at Newbury (3m, heavy) in February; that latest form has worked out well and he retains the same mark; firmly in calculations.

stable_tour.quote: He came from Guillaume Macaire towards the back end of last season. He's rated 124 and he did have some solid French form when winning twice at Auteuil, but that tailed off a bit, and our job is to try to rekindle that. The obvious thing seems to be to go chasing with him. He's come in looking great and we're very much looking forward to a winter campaign. 21-10-25

prev_owners.owner: Mrs S Russell & A M Russell

runners.comment: Fairly encouraging fourth over C&D in January last time but needs to build on that today
runners.spotlight: 0-8 since winning his first three starts in the 2023-24 season; still only six and he was a fairly encouraging fourth of 13 over C&D in January last time, but needs to build on that run if he's to threaten today.

quotes.race: Carlisle Junior "National Hunt" Hurdle
quotes.quote: We've had several of our nicer juveniles aimed at these races, but Rocheval is probably the loveliest one we've had. I loved the way he went through the race, especially after making a mistake at the second-last - Peter Scudamore, assistant trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's had a few injury niggles since his good three-year-old campaign. We've done some work on his back over the summer and that's really unlocked a bit of improvement. He looks potentially well handicapped for staying hurdles. 29-10-25

runners.comment: Inconsistent this term but ran pretty well two starts ago, and also in this race last year
runners.spotlight: Inconsistent this season and down the field at Haydock a fortnight ago; however, he ran pretty well when runner-up at Doncaster two starts ago and is 2lb lower than when a close fourth of 13 in this race last year; if he's on song in a first-time tongue-tie he might not be far away.

quotes.race: Sky Bet Club Handicap Hurdle (Go North Cab On Target Series Qualifier)
quotes.quote: I'm not sure about the decision, there's been softer bumps that have been awarded a race. It definitely put me off my stride, but they told me the winning distance was too far - Ryan Mania, jockey of I Am Max.

stable_tour.quote: Perhaps it's been a blessing that he fell on his chase debut at Wetherby as he's going to be much more mature when he goes chasing next season. Since then I've been delighted with him on his two runs back over hurdles with second-place finishes at Kelso and Haydock. I was slightly disappointed with the stewards' inquiry at Haydock as they cautioned the winning jockey but didn't change the result. He's a really tough horse who wants softer ground. We'll find a decent 3m hurdle for him now, possibly a Pertemps qualifier. 22-01-25

runners.comment: Stayed on strongly over 2m4f on handicap debut and this trip could be right up his street
runners.spotlight: 3m point winner who showed promise in novice/maiden hurdles here earlier in the year (2m/2m3f, soft) and stayed on strongly when 13l seventh of 19 on handicap debut at Down Royal (2m4f, yielding) last month; remains lightly raced and this step up in trip could be right up his street.

runners.owner: Toby Cole & Stars Of The Box
runners.comment: Ran well in fourth on handicap debut at Wetherby and further improvement is possible
runners.spotlight: Point winner who got off the mark over hurdles at the third attempt at Catterick (3m1f, soft) in February and was beaten only 4l when fourth on last month's handicap debut at Wetherby (3m, good to soft); unexposed and further improvement is possible.

stable_tour.quote: We didn't get a clear run with him last year, but he ran well on his first start over hurdles at Doncaster in January. He'll be going over fences, but should be able to make his mark in a maiden hurdle over an extended trip first. 18-11-25

runners.breeder: E A R L Haras De Montaigu
runners.comment: Well handicapped on form as recent as last March but unable to pose a threat this season
runners.spotlight: Very well handicapped on staying form as recent as last March and it's possible the step back up in trip will be a positive; however, unable to pose a threat across his six runs this season and has to raise his game.

quotes.race: Virgin Bet Daily Extra Places Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Patriotik is a good jumper and he enjoyed the drying ground. We ran him over three miles at Haydock and he unseated, and we've been desperate to try him again at the trip - Isabel Williams, rider.

stable_tour.quote: I have to say he's been disappointing this season, considering how well he ran on two occasions in March last year. It's nothing I can put my finger on either and we might try headgear. I had hoped to send him chasing by now but he'll stick to hurdling until he can find his real self. When that happens, chasing will be his game. He's a really good jumper who doesn't want it too deep. 14-01-26

runners.comment: Very lightly raced mare who could appreciate the step up in trip on handicap debut
runners.spotlight: Placed in a 3m point and she got off the mark at the third attempt over hurdles in a mares' novice here (2m4f, soft) last month; did it nicely from a solid yardstick and she's from the family of Paisley Park, so could appreciate the step up in trip on handicap debut; possible player.

stable_tour.quote: She finished her race very nicely at Kelso. That was over an inadequate trip and she'll be much better over further. 21-11-24

runners.comment: Up in grade after narrow Hereford win but he's unexposed at this sort of distance
runners.spotlight: He's done well since joining this yard and was having his first crack at a staying trip when winning over 3m1f at Hereford last month; did it only narrowly and is 3lb higher in a hotter race today, but he might have more to offer over this sort of distance.

quotes.race: Hereford Bull Trail Launch 2026 Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: The first time I rode Don Rafael was at Southwell and I got off thinking he wants a big galloping track. I then rode him here last time when he was third and felt going up in trip would suit him. He just seems to love this track and the nippiness of turning around the corners. They were in their own little battle in front, which worked out well for me. I was able to get a little fill into him, have one go after the last and he stuck every bit of it out. - Benjamin Macey, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

runners.comment: Two C&D wins in January but this 10yo may be vulnerable back up in grade
runners.spotlight: Course specialist who won two in a row over C&D (heavy/soft) in January; he's better than he showed when 15l third over C&D (soft) in February and the subsequent break may have helped, but this 10yo may still be vulnerable back up in grade.

racecards.verdict: Having caught the eye with a strong finish over 2m4f at Down Royal, this step up in trip could be just what IRISH CHAMP (nap) needs.
racecards.betting_forecast: 4/1 Woodland Park, 6/1 Hidden History, 7/1 Alentejo, 15/2 Hawthorn Street, 10/1 Draco Malfoy,  Kent De Thaix, 12/1 Society Soldier, 14/1 Billy Boi Blue,  Irish Champ,  Don Rafael, 16/1 I Am Max, 20/1 Just Ennemi,  Rocheval,  Shoeshine Boy, 25/1 Eyed,  Whistle Stop Tour,  Patriotik

racecards.race_name: Jardine Utilities Race To Repair 'Hands & Heels' Handicap Hurdle (Conditional/Amateurs') (RE Series)

prev_owners.owner: This Horse Is For Sale Partnership

runners.comment: Hit with a 10lb hike for latest 19l win at Newbury, but he's a 6yo firmly on the up
runners.spotlight: Ridden by Aamilah Aswat in his last five races; he's won the last two, though a 19l margin of victory at Newbury last time (2m4f, good to soft; first-time tongue-tie) provided the handicapper with the ammunition to hit him with a 10lb hike; he still rates a likely contender as a 6yo firmly on the up.

quotes.race: West Berkshire Mencap Conditional Jockeys' Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: Guchen ran brilliantly for me and he's always a lovely spin. He jumped really well and I couldn't have asked for any better. There was plenty left in the tank. I didn't want to look back so I just thought to keep going - Aamilah Aswat, jockey.

runners.breeder: H Lair,  J Lair &  F Champion
runners.comment: Perhaps handicapped on the high side but capable of having some say after a break
runners.spotlight: Won a bumper for Paul Nicholls and added a 2m4f handicap at Perth in October (soft) on his first run for Olly Murphy; ran well afterwards over 2m5f, and 3m was perhaps too far when last seen three months ago; he could be handicapped on the high side but capable of having some say.

quotes.race: Unibet Open National Hunt Flat Race (Category 1 Elimination) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Kap Boy is a nice, big baby. He'll be a future chaser one day, but we'll look after him and give him a couple more runs this season. McFabulous and Knappers Hill have won this race and it's a good race to run in and progress. We could find a nice race for him in the spring, there's plenty of improvement to come from him. Paul Nicholls, trainer

stable_tour.quote: Harry [Cobden] thought he'd gone wrong when pulling him up on his hurdling debut at Chepstow, but he came back 100 per cent sound. He must have knocked something, but it didn't affect him for long. He'll reappear in another novice hurdle soon. This is something of an in-between season for this big baby, as he's a future chaser plying his trade over hurdles this winter, so we'll continue to look after him. 04-11-24

runners.comment: His early-season form (2m3f-2m7f) offers encouragement off this mark
runners.spotlight: His early-season form (2m3f-2m7f) offers encouragement off this mark; last two runs well below his best, though heavy ground was a feasible excuse the last time when a tongue-tie joined his regular cheekpieces; hard to rule out.

stable_tour.quote: The ground was a bit quick when he finished tailed off on his chase debut up at Ayr in April. We ran him back over hurdles first time up and he surprised us when winning nicely at Fontwell last month; we'll now look for something similar in the next couple of weeks and keep him to hurdling for the time being. 04-11-25

runners.comment: This 5yo may need to be on a sharp upward curve if he's to defy this initial mark
runners.spotlight: Had them well strung out in a 2m Southwell maiden (soft) in early March but that was a modest contest, for all that the second and third horses have won since, in low-grade races on the Flat and over hurdles; this 5yo may need to be on a sharp upward curve if he's to defy this initial mark.

runners.comment: Ready winner of a Wexford handicap on debut for these connections; a hood is added
runners.spotlight: Narrowly denied in a Gowran handicap (2m, heavy) before changing hands for £21,000; hit the ground running for this yard when readily taking a 2m handicap on soft at Wexford; should have no trouble staying this far and a hood goes on; he's not yet exposed and quite interesting.

runners.comment: Last year's winner who goes well fresh, so a 75-day break is probably a good thing
runners.spotlight: Narrow winner of this 12 months ago when 10lb lower; has shown that he can deal with this high a mark and he goes well fresh, so a 75-day break after being below par last time is probably a good thing; respected.

quotes.race: Racing Post Go North Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: Summergrounds is a consistent little horse and he loves this ground. Danny gave him a great ride, they were getting at it and he just took his time - Nicky Richards, trainer.

runners.breeder: Sarl Igep Haras Du Chateau De Rabodanges
runners.comment: Unseated four out last time at Wincanton and in career-best form prior to that
runners.spotlight: Goes on all ground; unseated four out when favourite at Wincanton last time; had been in career-best form with a win at Wincanton (1m7f) and a second at Taunton (2m3f); even more needed here, however.

quotes.race: Racing Excellence Conditional Jockeys' Training Series Handicap Hurdle (Part Of The RE Series)
quotes.quote: Thankyouandplease didn't come off the bridle. I've always thought a lot of him but it didn't go his way at Plumpton. He's in the zone at home, so we got him back out quickly, and we'll do the same again as he can go off 95 at Exeter next Thursday. He's in at Taunton [on Thursday] and it's tempting, but the ground would be too quick for him. Logically, a bit of time to Exeter should help and he can go in again hopefully. We've been knocking on the door, hopefully we're hitting a purple patch now and he can add to it next week - Syd Hosie, trainer.

runners.comment: Ran surprisingly well over 3m last time at Wincanton when all his form is over shorter
runners.spotlight: Without a win since 2023 but he has dropped to a dangerous mark and ran surprisingly well over 3m last time at Wincanton when all his form is over shorter; goes on soft.

quotes.race: Champion Hats Juvenile Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: It's taken a while for the penny to drop. Balboa has had two runs but he still had a look at the first (hurdle). We got a bit of good fortune with the non-runners but that's racing and you've got to kick the ball when it's in front of you. He's ok and he's solid, he seems to handle the soft ground. We might turn up at the Cheltenham meeting in November, although we do have some higher rated who could go there. Milton Harris, trainer

stable_tour.quote: He's a winner waiting to happen. He's fairly typical, in that he had a good juvenile season and then probably paid for that a little bit as he was a little overrated when he started last season. He ran very respectably at Taunton the other day when a good fourth in a close finish. He's in at Doncaster on Friday and I would envisage him running well over 2m4f or 3m this spring and getting his head in front at some stage again. 21-01-26

runners.comment: In the new cheekpieces he jumped well and won unchallenged at Newcastle; up 9lb
runners.spotlight: The first-time cheekpieces appeared to make a huge difference at Newcastle (2m1f, good to soft) where he jumped well in front and won unchallenged by just over 5l; 9lb higher in a higher grade but he arrives here a relative unknown quantity, especially over this far.

runners.comment: It's never ideal being 5lb out of the weights in this competitive a handicap
runners.spotlight: Exposed five-time winner who ran perfectly well back from an absence at Carlisle but it's never ideal being 5lb out of the weights in this competitive a handicap.

quotes.race: Get Daily Tips At racingtv.com Handicap Hurdle (Go North Middle Distance Series Qualifier) (Div I)
quotes.quote: Rickety Gate took a little time to win. He might jump a fence a time as he jumped tidy enough there - Nicky Richards, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: A solid handicap hurdler who won two races last season and should win another couple this time. He had a bad fall at Doncaster last season and it took a couple of runs to get his confidence back. He's looking good now and will run soon, as long as the ground isn't too soft. 25-10-23

racecards.verdict: The now-hooded WESTOFTIGNES is trained in Ireland but owned by a Scotsman and he did it pretty easily on his debut for this yard.
racecards.betting_forecast: 5/2 Nice One Eric, 100/30 Guchen, 6/1 Westoftignes, 7/1 Kap Boy, 8/1 Travis Wheatley, 12/1 Summergrounds,  Thankyouandplease,  Balboa, 14/1 Paso Doble, 16/1 Rickety Gate

racecards.race_name: Blackmore Build And Design Handicap

runners.owner: S Packham, A Austin And B Austin
runners.comment: Has struggled under both codes for some time and he's hard to trust at the moment
runners.spotlight: Listed Flat winner for Aidan O'Brien; made a successful hurdle debut for this yard in early 2024 but it's been a struggle since then under both codes; has dropped a long way in the weights but he's hard to trust at the moment and others are preferred.

quotes.race: Virgin Bet Daily Extra Places Novices' Hurdle (Novices' Championship Hurdle Series Qual') (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I expected Peking Opera to run very well but I've had two good horses run in this race in the last two years and they were beaten. He's always been a bit lazy at home but is a different horse in the track. You could work him with a donkey and he'd be quite happy to work with it. I thought given his Flat form he'd want a stiff two miles but he's shown he's got a bit of pace. He'll probably run in the Adonis at Kempton next - Gary Moore, trainer.

quotes.race: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Yeats Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: Peking Opera has done well over the winter and is a horse that is going to stay very well. He could be one for something like the Queen's Vase over 1m6f at Ascot. You could bring him back a fraction to 1m4f. He has good options and he did well to win on seasonal debut - Chris Armstrong, stable's representative.

quotes.race: Irish Stallion Farms EBF (C & G) Maiden
quotes.quote: Peking Opera had a lovely run on his debut at Naas, and his work has stepped up since. Seamus gave him a lovely ride. It's nice to get a win with him as a two-year-old and he'll be a horse to look forward to next year over a trip. That might be him done for the year, we'll see how he comes out of it - Chris Armstrong, representing Aidan O'Brien.

stable_tour.quote: He won a Listed race at Navan last time and stays well. He came out of that in good order and the Queen's Vase is definitely a possibility for him. 15-06-23

He looked good on his first start over hurdles at Sandown but he was getting a lot of weight from his rivals and then he fell at the last when beaten in the Adonis. He's been disappointing in four runs on the Flat but should be suited by stepping up in trip in handicap hurdles. 29-10-24

prev_owners.owner: HM The King & HM The Queen

runners.comment: Flopped at Newcastle latest but that was a Class 3 and has claims if he can bounce back
runners.spotlight: Triple turf winner who finished well to go close off this mark at Kempton (2m, AW) in January; flopped with a heavy defeat at Newcastle the following month but that was a Class 3 and has claims if he can bounce back after a short break; has form on good to firm and good to soft.

quotes.race: Download The Racecourse App Raceday Ready Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
quotes.quote: They bought Educator as a three-year-old off William Haggas. He ran well for Mick Appleby, but he was running over a mile-six and two miles, and I always thought he seemed to have a bit more speed - Brendan Powell, assistant trainer, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

quotes.race: Radcliffe & Co Handicap
quotes.quote: We've always thought of Educator as a pretty decent horse and still think at home there are great signs of him being a pretty decent animal, he just needs racing now. He'll strip much fitter next time and be more focused. When he won, we thought he should have won further - we thought we were ahead of the handicapper, but he only does enough. William had him in the Derby early on and we felt he was a stakes-level horse - John Warren, royal racing adviser.

quotes.race: bet365 Handicap
quotes.quote: It's great to win with a homebred such as Educator in these colours. He's in everything but it could well be that he needs a mile and a half - William Haggas, trainer.

quotes.race: Mike James Occasionals Memorial EBF Novice Stakes (Colts & Geldings)
quotes.quote: Educator is well-bred and had experience over the rest of the field. He wore cheekpieces for the first time just to help him travel a little bit better into the race. It took him a while to get going, but as soon as I asked him, he picked up well and hit the line very strongly. He gave me a proper feel, he's a really nice horse with a good temperament. He's improving with each run and is going to get better with racing. He's got a big frame to fill as well and is going to be exciting for next year - Cieren Fallon, jockey.

runners.comment: Hard to predict but he's on a workable mark back on the Flat and conditions should be fine
runners.spotlight: Turned things around back over hurdles with a win at Ludlow (2m, good) in November but he was a well-held third in a small field at Sedgefield the following month; bit to prove again after that but conditions should be fine back in this sphere and he's well treated on his close call at Chester last autumn; not ruled out on his return.

runners.breeder: Lynn Lodge Stud & Pier House Stud
runners.comment: In fair form on AW this spring but he hasn't won since 2023; needs to find more
runners.spotlight: Veteran who hasn't won since 2023 but he's been in fair form on AW this spring including when fourth on Polytrack (2m) in his last two starts; should be in the mix again but he needs to find more to make a big impact; cheekpieces are removed and blinkers return.

quotes.race: Christmas Party Nights At Dundalk Stadium Maiden
quotes.quote: Bashful Boy showed a good turn of foot and saw out the trip well after running a cracker here last time. He was genuine and hit the line well - John Feane, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's had a good summer on the Flat and over hurdles and he ran above expectations on soft ground when fourth in the Cesarewitch. However, the ground was probably too bad for him at Cheltenham on Saturday, when he was pulled up. I'd been hoping that stepping up in trip would eke out a little more improvement and I'd like to try three miles again when we can. 31-10-23

runners.comment: Six wins on turf but all over shorter trips and he's been quiet on AW this winter
runners.spotlight: Often a front-runner but he's a tactically versatile; six wins on turf (1m4f-1m6f) but he's not easy to predict and has been quiet on AW this winter; now only 1lb higher than for his last success but he still has stamina to prove at this trip and others are preferred.

quotes.race: Thorn Baker Allianz Xenia Bath Summer Stayers' Series Final Handicap
quotes.quote: It was brilliant as we thought the ground may have gone slightly against us but I suppose Lusaka missing the start helped him a little bit to get into the race - John Flint, trainer.

runners.comment: Dual course winner and he needs watching in market back on the Flat on his return
runners.spotlight: Has done a lot of his winning in Jersey but he scored here (1m5f, firm) in the autumn and was runner-up over hurdles at Taunton (2m3f) in his final run in 2025; returns after 141 days off but he needs watching in market back on the Flat.

quotes.race: NB Surfacing Handicap
quotes.quote: Man Of The Sea won well. Mr Mulholland said before the race he was in great form. He was a bit outpaced the last day at Windsor but he stays all day. He pinged the gates, I kept hold of him and he ran all the way to the line - George Rooke, rider.

quotes.race: Come Racing 11th November Nursery Handicap (Plus 10 Race)
quotes.quote: Man Of The Sea jumped and travelled, I was able to sit off the good pace and when I got stuck into him he saw it out to the line. He has plenty of experience and it stood to him. He did it well and hopefully there's another day in him - Billy Lee, rider

runners.owner: R Miles, V Miles, T Stamp & Partner

prev_owners.owner: S Barton, T Stamp, R Miles, & Partner

runners.comment: Nine-time AW winner but he's struggled in his six runs on turf; opposable
runners.spotlight: Got back on the scoresheet at Lingfield (2m, AW) last month and he ran to a similar level when fourth at Wolverhampton (1m6f) 11 days ago; on lower mark back on turf but he's struggled in his six runs in this sphere including three 2m handicaps; risks attached.

quotes.race: BetUK. Home Of The Acca Handicap
quotes.quote: The Craftymaster has been a revelation. He used to be slow, but stayed. Now, when that was going to turn into a sprint, I was thinking you can't go wide as you'll never win, so just wait and see if you outstay them. He's put them to bed in half a furlong with his injection of speed. He's learning and getting better at everything he does. This was the first test of his mettle, a full field with horses who have been in very good form and he's up to it. I don't feel I'm at the bottom of him yet - I feel if something came at him he'd go again -  William Carson, jockey, speaking on Sky Sports Racing.

quotes.race: BetUK. It's Where The UK Bets Handicap
quotes.quote: The Craftymaster has developed late and we've been very lucky to have him. He's progressing really nicely. He's going up the grades slowly and he's coping with it. He stays very well and he's lazy through his races, so you'd like to think there's always just a tiny little bit left. We'll keep going forward - Tony Carroll, trainer, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

racecards.verdict: Preference is for NO MORE BOLERO who won over hurdles on his penultimate run and looks well handicapped back on the Flat.
racecards.betting_forecast: 5/2 No More Bolero, 3/1 Man Of The Sea, 9/2 Bashful Boy, 11/2 The Craftymaster, 6/1 Educator, 10/1 Peking Opera, 12/1 Lusaka

racecards.race_name: Blackmore Building Contractors British EBF Fillies' Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands C/D) (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Non runner
runners.spotlight: Non runner.

runners.comment: Has plenty of speed in pedigree and she needs checking in market on debut
runners.spotlight: Fourth foal; half-sister to Italian 6f/6.5f winner Vento D'Irlande; dam French Listed-placed 5.5f 2yo winner (RPR 81), half-sister to Italian 7f Listed winner Ziggy's Dream, out of Listed-placed 1m1f/9.4f winner; has plenty of speed in pedigree and she needs checking in market on debut.

runners.comment: 30,000gns yearling; plenty to like on paper and she's an interesting newcomer
runners.spotlight: 30,000gns yearling; second foal; dam 5.7f/6f winner (including 2yo; RPR 92), half-sister to winners Jacob Black (useful 7f/1m), Blood Moon (5f/6f including 2yo) and Ta Ajaab (Swedish 6f), out of 5f 2yo winner; plenty to like on paper and she's an interesting newcomer.

runners.comment: Has speed and stamina in pedigree and market should guide on debut
runners.spotlight: Second foal; half-sister to 5f/6f 2yo winner Brightling (RPR 56); dam 6f winner (81), half-sister to winners Rwenearlytheredad (5f-1m), Goldenhurst (5.7f 2yo) and Elysian Lady (French 11.5f), out of half-sister to 5f 2yo Group 2 winner Langs Lash; has speed and stamina in pedigree and market should guide on debut.

runners.comment: 28,000euros yearling; yard won the Brocklesby and she needs a close look on debut
runners.spotlight: 28,000euros yearling; eighth foal; half-sister to winners Conglomerate (UAE 1m dirt; RPR 98), Jolt (7f 2yo; 89), Raven's Applause (6f; 77), Conformist (Canadian 6f dirt including 2yo/stakes) and Lew's Skyhook (US 6.5f dirt); dam US 6f dirt winner; yard won the Brocklesby last month and she needs a close look on debut.

runners.comment: Has useful pedigree and interesting to see how she figures in market
runners.spotlight: 21,000gns yearling; third foal; closely related to 6f winner Candy (including 2yo Listed; RPR 104); dam unplaced 6f, sister to prolific 5f/6f winner Danzeno (including Group 3), half-sister to 5f Listed winner Demora; has a useful pedigree and interesting to see how she figures in market.

runners.comment: Well-related filly and yard was 15% with 2yos last year; in the mix on debut
runners.spotlight: 35,000euros yearling; half-sister to six winners including Orazio (6f including 2yo/Listed placed; RPR 114), Ten Pounds (6f/7f; 111) and Suits You (6f/7f including 2yo Listed/France/HK; 103); dam 7f AW winner (98); yard 15% with 2yos last year and she's in the mix on debut.

runners.comment: Bred for speed and interesting to see how she figures in market
runners.spotlight: 9,000gns yearling; first foal; dam 5f 2yo winner (RPR 71), sister to 5.7f winner Elland Road Girl, half-sister to 5f 2yo Listed winner Rocket Rodney, out of once-raced sister to 6f 2yo Group 2 winner Mister Cosmi; bred for speed and interesting to see how she figures in market.

runners.comment: Yard 3-49 with 2yos last year and others look more likely
runners.spotlight: 17,000gns yearling, resold 7,000gns yearling; first foal; dam unraced close relative of 5f 2yo Group 3 winner Steel Bull, out of maiden sister to 5f/5.7f winner Marietta Robusti, half-sister to 5f 2yo Listed winner Three Sea Captains; yard 3-49 with 2yos last year and others look more likely.

runners.comment: Got upset in the preliminaries before finishing a well-held seventh of ten on C&D debut
runners.spotlight: Got upset in the preliminaries before finishing a well-held seventh of ten on C&D debut (good; 22-1) two weeks ago; passed over.

runners.comment: Yard 2-36 with 2yos last year and she could be one for later on
runners.spotlight: 12,000gns yearling; sister to 5f/6f AW winner Colors Of Freedom (including 2yo; RPR 67), half-sister to 6f winner Scarboroughwarning (86); dam 5f winner (including 2yo; 93), out of half-sister to 6f 2yo Group 3 winner Polar Bird; yard 2-36 with 2yos last year and she could be one for later on.

runners.comment: Finished down the field at Wolverhampton but she's a likely improver on her second start
runners.spotlight: Well-held sixth of eight on Wolverhampton debut (AW) 11 days ago but she looked inexperienced and should know much more this time; likely improver and she's not ruled for yard that won this in 2023 and 2024.

runners.comment: Never got involved in the Brocklesby and she needs to leave that form well behind
runners.spotlight: 2,000gns yearling; never dangerous when in midfield in the Brocklesby (good to soft; 25-1) and she needs to leave that form well behind.

runners.comment: Could be a longer-term prospect on pedigree and others are preferred
runners.spotlight: 11,000gns yearling; eleventh foal; half-sister to four winners including Ibiza Rocks (7f 2yo; RPR 94), I Still Have Faith (1m-1m2f Flat, 91; 2m hurdle) and No More Thrills (7f AW; 80); dam Listed-placed 5f 2yo winner (98); could be a longer-term prospect on pedigree and others are preferred.

runners.comment: Quite a bit to like on paper and she's in the mix on debut
runners.spotlight: Bungle Inthejungle filly; 14,000euros yearling; second foal; dam unraced half-sister to winners Gossamer Seed (7f Group 3) and Questi Amori (Italian 5f/6f including 2yo); quite a bit to like on paper and she's in the mix on debut.

runners.comment: Yard 0-6 with 2yos this season and she could be one for further down the line
runners.spotlight: £16,000 yearling; half-sister to winners Pull The Rug (6f 2yo; RPR 70) and Oldbury Lad (7f AW; 58); dam Listed-placed 6f/7f winner (including 2yo/AW; 99), half-sister to useful 1m/1m2f winner Tobar Na Gaoise; yard 0-6 with 2yos this season and she could be one for further down the line.

racecards.verdict: The market should be highly informative but at this stage the vote goes to Archie Watson's well-bred newcomer MADELEINE.

racecards.race_name: MJ Church Handicap

runners.comment: Made it 2-4 in cheekpieces with an emphatic win at Wolverhampton; respected under penalty
runners.spotlight: Won at Southwell for Mick Appleby in December and he made it 2-4 in cheekpieces with a dominant display at Wolverhampton (6f, AW) last week; record of 0-7 on turf but he ran well in big-field handicap at York last summer and he's a major player if he can transfer his progress back to this sphere; respected under a penalty.

runners.comment: Returns for new yard but he's on workable mark and needs watching in market; new headgear
runners.spotlight: Ended last season with a heavy defeat in the Ayr Bronze Cup but he did well for Hugo Palmer last summer including a brave win off this mark at Chester (6f, good); returns in new headgear for new yard but he went close on his reappearance last term and he needs watching in market.

quotes.race: TMT Group Handicap
quotes.quote: We ruined Arabian Cobra last year by running him in the Windsor Castle. It's taken a long time to get his confidence back. But this year working with the juveniles has got him back to himself. That was his second win in a week and if things went right I wouldn't rule out his winning again - Hugo Palmer, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's had a really good year but he never raised a gallop in the Ayr Bronze Cup though, and I don't know why. It's a tough ask for a three-year-old in the older-horse handicaps but we thought it would suit him. He likes give in the ground and it was frustrating. He's in the sales. 08-10-25

runners.comment: AW specialist but he's on a lower mark on turf and has possibilities back in this sphere
runners.spotlight: Nine-time AW winner who won three in a row during the winter and was a creditable fifth in Class 3 at Lingfield (6f, Polytrack) two weeks ago; record of 1-21 on turf but he's on a lower mark in this sphere and he had a close call at Windsor last autumn; dangerous.

runners.comment: Dual course winner who is versatile ground-wise and she needs a close look on return
runners.spotlight: Six-time turf winner who has a good record at Bath and is only 2lb higher than for her win here (5f, heavy) last autumn; returns after 165 days off but she went close on her reappearance last season and that was on good to firm at Chepstow (6f); in the mix.

quotes.race: Extra Place Races At Fitzdares.com Fillies' Handicap
quotes.quote: Jax Edge was in front far too early but it was a brave, topweight-carrying performance - Gina Mangan, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

runners.comment: Well treated on old form and it wouldn't be a surprise if he made a bold bid back on turf
runners.spotlight: Both wins were on turf in 2024 but he's well treated on old form and has run respectably on Tapeta (5f/6f) in last two starts; can make the running and it wouldn't be a surprise if he made a bold bid back in this sphere.

runners.comment: Triple C&D winner who scored at Wolverhampton last month; respected back on turf
runners.spotlight: Triple C&D winner who scored on her reappearance at Wolverhampton last month and was a close third there 18 days ago; on same mark as for that last run and she's respected back at this track; handles most ground but her turf wins have been on good to firm/firm.

runners.comment: All three wins have been on AW and this is competitive back on turf; others preferred
runners.spotlight: All three wins have been on AW and she ran right up to her best when a close fourth at Wolverhampton (5f) last month; on same mark here but she's 0-9 on turf and this is highly competitive back in this sphere; others are more persuasive.

runners.comment: Usually seen at a lower level and he has some work to do after 199 days off
runners.spotlight: Won at Chester last summer but that was off 5lb lower and he was never involved here (5f. good to firm) in his final run last season; usually seen at a lower level and he has some work to do after 199 days off; one of two runners for yard.

quotes.race: Halliwell Jones Handicap (Div I)
quotes.quote: Finley's [Marsh] given Aces Wild a fantastic ride and it's great to see him doing well. The horse deserved it. He'd been unlucky as we'd been chasing pots on the AW and things just hadn't fallen right. The track was a bit of a question mark but he's done well around tight tracks on the AW, so we thought it was worth a try - and it's paid off. Our horses are coming back into great form now and he ran well last time, so I'm glad to see him win - Adrian Wintle, trainer.

quotes.race: Join Us On Instagram @dundalk_stadium Maiden
quotes.quote: Aces Wild is a fast little horse and he's lightly raced and those kind of sprinters improve with age. We are hopeful he will keep the ball rolling - John McConnell, trainer

runners.breeder: S Emmet And Miss R Emmet
runners.owner: S Emmet And Miss R Emmet
runners.comment: His last win was in 2024 and was well held on his reappearance last April; reservations
runners.spotlight: Four-time turf winner but his last success was in July 2024; well handicapped on his best form last season but he's not easy to predict and was well held on his seasonal return last April; some reservations.

stable_tour.quote: He ran in the Grey Horse Handicap at Newmarket on Saturday. It's a race he has won before and the owners wanted to win it again but it was a strong renewal and he could only manage midfield. The ground had been watered too, which didn't help. He's getting on in years and his handicap mark is dropping as he gets older. But he's a dear friend of the yard and a joy to have around. He's thoroughly genuine and may turn out at Windsor on Saturday. 20-08-25

runners.comment: Five-time turf winner who ran well on his reappearance at Kempton; in the mix back in trip
runners.spotlight: Five of his six wins (5f/6f) have been on turf but he returned after five months off with a fair third at Kempton (7f) three weeks ago; should benefit from that run and he has possibilities on this drop back in trip.

stable_tour.quote: He had lost all his confidence. He had a foot injury, which left him a bit sore for a while, but once he had dropped in grade and we were able to run him in one of the novice rider races with no whips, he won easily and got his confidence back again. He's potentially still well handicapped on his best form but hasn't really come back to his good three-year-old form just yet. 27-08-25

runners.comment: Won four times last year and he has possibilities if this sets up for his closing style
runners.spotlight: Hold-up performer who won four times last year including off 4lb higher at Brighton (7f, good to firm); two solid efforts on AW since rejoining Tony Carroll last month and he could be a big factor if he gets the breaks back on turf; tongue-tie and blinkers are removed but he has won without headgear.

quotes.race: knees.co.uk Home And Electrical 145th Anniversary Handicap
quotes.quote: Jack [Doughty] gave Mumayaz a lovely ride. He's been consistent all year. He had a great all-weather campaign and we've been very pleased with him - Tony Carroll, trainer.

quotes.race: Grant Thornton Nursery Handicap
quotes.quote: Mumayaz was planned to sit in the first three but they went very hard and I rode him with confidence. He's quite versatile and we've always liked him, he seems to have turned a corner. He's an honest horse - Chris Hayes, rider.

runners.comment: All ten wins have been on turf and she handles most ground; market informative on return
runners.spotlight: All ten wins have been on turf and latest was at Chepstow last September; handles most ground but she ended last season on a low note and she didn't shine on her reappearance last spring; market should guide after 179 days off.

quotes.race: HAC Plumbing Supplies Fillies' Handicap
quotes.quote: Connie's Rose loves racing - there is no mare tougher.  She has a good routine at home - she doesn't do a lot or see another horse - and she's a joy to train.  I'm still undecided if she prefers 5f.  We thought she was going to be a 1m-plus horse as she was slow, green and didn't know how to gallop at all, but she got a lot quicker at home.  Would we get more improvement holding her up at 1m?  We don't know.  We may try it in future but we don't want to change anything that's working at the moment - Grace Harris, trainer, speaking to Racing TV.

racecards.verdict: An open race in which the vote goes to HUNKY DORY who made it 2-4 in cheekpieces with a dominant display at Wolverhampton last week.

racecards.race_name: Wight Event Toilets Hire Handicap

runners.comment: Shaped with huge promise at Lingfield 14 days ago; must be well treated judged on that run
runners.spotlight: Ready winner of a 5f novice at Wolverhampton in February; plenty went wrong on his handicap debut at Southwell and it was a mighty effort when a close third at Lingfield on Good Friday (6f) given he was hampered at the start, unsettled as a result and then forced extremely wide throughout; surely well handicapped and displayed promise on good to firm on debut.

runners.comment: 5f turf win last June; encouraging seasonal return last month; not ruled out
runners.spotlight: Returned from seven months off (gelded during his absence) with a dead-heat for second at Wolverhampton last month (6f); his win came on good to firm and this extended 5f should suit; not discounted.

runners.comment: 5f AW win when last seen in October; not obviously well treated but he is unexposed
runners.spotlight: Improved with each of his three runs last autumn, getting off the mark when switched to AW at Newcastle in October (5f); his opening mark looks a tough one but he is at least unexposed.

runners.comment: Beaten favourite on nursery debut (7f) but ran okay; down in trip for this return; gelded
runners.spotlight: He beat 13 rivals when winning a Kempton novice (7f) last September; beaten favourite but ran creditably on his nursery debut at Newmarket when last seen in October; gelded since; drops in trip for his reappearance and with a good 7lb claimer enlisted.

runners.breeder: Lynch Bages, Camas Park & Summerhill B/S
runners.comment: Improved his RPR with each of his 2yo runs, beaten a nose on latest start; handicap debut
runners.spotlight: Steady progress with each of his four 2yo runs, beaten a nose a Wolverhampton in October (6f); could progress further now handicapping.

runners.comment: Just behind Alvin at Lingfield two weeks ago; vulnerable to less exposed rivals
runners.spotlight: Drawn widest when a close fourth at Lingfield on Good Friday but still enjoyed a much better trip than third-placed Alvin; may struggle to reverse those placings.

quotes.race: PricedUp Daily Sports Boosts Nursery Handicap (Jockey Club Grassroots Nursery Qualifier)
quotes.quote: I was a bit worried as I could see them adjusting the saddle behind the stalls and Hollie [Doyle, jockey] was out of sight, so for a second I thought Akabusi was going to be a non-runner. Hollie said he was going down to post beautifully, but then he just jinked to the side and she came off, and he kicked her in the leg as she went down. We always felt that once he'd been gelded he'd put his best feet forward. He's sharpened up at home and is starting to show it on the track too - Michael Keady, trainer.

runners.comment: Had a good year already but vulnerable to less exposed rivals back on turf
runners.spotlight: Four AW wins for this yard in the winter; made a bold bid from the front at Lingfield on Good Friday before weakening into sixth; his two best turf runs came on soft and good.

runners.comment: Hasn't lived up to market billing in two handicap runs; should do better at some point
runners.spotlight: Narrow winner of a 6f AW maiden last September; hasn't lived up to market billing in two handicap runs; should do better at some point but others appeal more today.

runners.breeder: W H R John And Partners
runners.comment: On the up when last seen but in small-field 5f nurseries; this is tougher on stable debut
runners.spotlight: Ended his time with Archie Watson in good form, winning a couple of small-field 5f nurseries; sold for 21,000gns in October; in deeper waters for his seasonal/stable debut.

runners.comment: Maiden win came on soft; not obviously well treated; apprentice having first ride
runners.spotlight: His maiden win came on soft ground and he is untried on faster than good; fourth to Akabusi when last seen in October suggests he's vulnerable, and he has an inexperienced apprentice booked.

runners.comment: Stayed on for fourth on recent stable debut; stepping back up in trip looks  a plus
runners.spotlight: Didn't really progress for William Haggas after winning a 6f Yarmouth maiden on her second start; late headway into fourth on her stable debut at Wolverhampton last month; better can be expected back up in trip today.

runners.comment: Course winner (5f, soft) last September but returns from an absence off a tough mark
runners.spotlight: Won small-field 5f handicap on soft ground here last September; stiff task at Goodwood 11 days later; absent since and looks on a tough mark.

runners.comment: Similar form in three 2yo runs; improvement essential now handicapping
runners.spotlight: Recorded an RPR of 71 in each of his three 2yo runs; gelded during his absence; looks on a tough opening mark.

runners.comment: Struggled in two nurseries last autumn but promise last spring and he's had a wind op
runners.spotlight: Promise on turf last spring; returned from a four-month break with two disappointing efforts in nurseries in the autumn; had a wind operation since last in action and still has time to deliver on that early promise.

stable_tour.quote: He's had three runs and ran well when third in a 6f maiden at Windsor  last time. He had a little problem, so he couldn't run when he was due to at Bath this month - he pulled a little muscle but he's fine now. I think we'll probably go to the Super Sprint with him. 02-07-25

runners.comment: Two good runs here in the autumn but he is upped in class for his return
runners.spotlight: Close second over C&D in September (good to firm) before digging deep to win a 5f nursery back here three weeks later (heavy); up in class for his return.

quotes.race: BeatWright: Beat The Wright Way Nursery Handicap
quotes.quote: Red Snapper really deserved that after his run here last time. It was a big question whether he'd like the ground, but we rolled the dice and he certainly finished off the best - Ben Ffrench Davis, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

racecards.verdict: To finish as close as he did having suffered such a wide trip at Lingfield strongly suggests that ALVIN (nap) is ahead of his mark.

racecards.race_name: Unibet Supports Bath Racecourse Restricted Maiden Stakes (Bands C/D) (GBB Race)

runners.owner: Mr H Maye and The Joe Tickle Racing Club
runners.comment: Finished last in two Flat maidens and was pulled up on hurdle/stable debut in December
runners.spotlight: Failed to beat a rival in two Flat maidens (1m, AW/good) for Stan Moore in the autumn and was pulled up on his stable/hurdle debut in December.

runners.comment: 150-1 and he finished a well-held seventh of 11 on Kempton debut (1m, AW) last week
runners.spotlight: 150-1 and he finished a well-held seventh of 11 on Kempton debut (1m, AW) last week; opposable.

runners.comment: Showed some promise when third at Southwell and he's open to more progress
runners.spotlight: Beaten a long way on 1m Southwell debut last month but he showed promise when third of nine over same C&D nine days later; this is a much tougher assignment but he has a good pedigree and is open to more progress on this switch to turf.

runners.comment: 11,000gns breeze-up 2yo; this is a tough starting point and he's probably best watched
runners.spotlight: 3,500euros foal, 7,000euros yearling, 11,000gns breeze-up 2yo; fourth foal; dam placed 1m2f 2yo (RPR 73), closely related to Australian 1m2f Group 3 winner Mask Of Time, out of 14.5f winning half-sister to 1,000 Guineas winner Miss France; this is a tough starting point and he's probably best watched.

runners.comment: Looks interesting on his debut third at Kempton (1m) and he's in the mix back in trip
runners.spotlight: Belied his 100-1 odds with keeping-on third of 13 at Kempton (1m, AW) in sole 2yo start; well held on reappearance at Doncaster (1m2f, good to soft) last month but that was a useful maiden and he's clear second-best on the figures in this line-up; in the mix back in trip.

runners.comment: No progress in three runs at up to 1m and minor handicaps will be more suitable
runners.spotlight: No progress in her three runs at up to 1m and has a best RPR of 55; minor handicaps will be more suitable after this and she's best watched.

runners.comment: 0-6 but she sets a useful standard back in much calmer waters and should be hard to beat
runners.spotlight: Six-race maiden but she finished placed in a fillies' Listed race at Newbury (7f, soft) in the autumn and wasn't beaten far in a conditions event at Kempton (1m, AW) on her return last month; sets a useful standard back in calmer waters and she should be hard to beat.

racecards.verdict: This looks a golden opportunity for OURBREN who sets a clear standard back in much calmer waters.
racecards.betting_forecast: 1/4 Ourbren, 4/1 Tough Date, 10/1 Miss Mambo, 25/1 Malakai Kite, 33/1 Ocean Force, 100/1 Lamlash

racecards.race_name: Silvershine Turf Services Handicap

runners.comment: Eighth in Southwell handicap latest; slowly away there and could do better on turf debut
runners.spotlight: Took a step forward on his return when second at Chelmsford (1m) but failed to build on it when eighth of nine in 1m Southwell handicap 15 days ago; slowly away there and could still do better on his first run on turf.

runners.comment: In good form, third in 1m Southwell handicap 48 days ago; must enter calculations
runners.spotlight: Advanced his form in a visor when bagging a pair of 1m handicaps at Wolverhampton and Newcastle in February; has continued in good form, third in 1m Southwell handicap 48 days ago; must enter calculations.

runners.comment: Won 7f Southwell novice in September; more to offer for in-form yard on her handicap debut
runners.spotlight: Confirmed the promise of her debut when winning a 7f Southwell novice in September; off since but she has more to offer for her in-form yard on her handicap debut.

runners.owner: M H Dixon & J L Rowsell
runners.comment: Good third in 1m1f Newmarket nursery in November; needs considering on her seasonal return
runners.spotlight: Got off the mark at the third attempt in 1m Leicester maiden in October and backed it up with a good third of six in 1m1f Newmarket nursery following month; she needs considering on her seasonal return.

runners.comment: Bagged 7f/1m nurseries at Kempton in October; remains on a workable mark so he's a player
runners.spotlight: Upwardly-mobile juvenile who bagged 7f/1m nurseries at Kempton in October; remains on a workable mark despite a 4lb rise and rates a player in his hat-trick bid.

runners.comment: Placed for Owen Burrows at 2yrs; failed to beat rival on yard debut at Doncaster on return
runners.spotlight: Placed on four runs (7f/1m) for Owen Burrows at 2yrs; changed hands for 25,000gns and gelded but failed to beat a rival on his stable debut in a 7f Doncaster novice 19 days ago.

runners.comment: 4th at Southwell/Wolverhampton in 2026; can take step forward now handicapping up in trip
runners.spotlight: Has shaped with some promise for her new stable (with Alice Haynes for debut) when fourth in a pair of 7f novices at Southwell and Wolverhampton in 2026; can take a step forward now handicapping up in trip.

runners.comment: Promising second at Kempton last month; can go well again with progress on the cards
runners.spotlight: Back from seven months off (also gelded) with a promising second of nine on his handicap debut at Kempton (1m) last month; up 1lb but he can go well again with further progress on the cards.

runners.comment: Keen-going fifth at Lingfield 78 days ago; hood on now and he remains with potential
runners.spotlight: Failed to build on earlier promise on his handicap debut when a keen-going fifth of six at Lingfield (1m) 78 days ago; hood goes on now after a break and he remains with potential.

runners.comment: Failed to improve with Kempton fourth in October; more needed if he's to get off the mark
runners.spotlight: Modest juvenile maiden who failed to improve on his nursery debut when fourth of six at Kempton (1m) in October; more is needed if he's to get off the mark at the fifth attempt here.

runners.comment: Debut Salisbury third; a big disappointment after so big step foward needed on h'cap debut
runners.spotlight: Shaped well when third in 7f novice at Salisbury on her debut but she proved a big disappointment after, ninth of ten in 7f Chelmsford novice on final run in 2025; this switch to handicaps needs to spark major progress.

racecards.verdict: Preference is for CHAPMAN'S PEAK who ended 2025 very much on the up with a pair of Kempton nursery wins. He can complete a hat-trick.
racecards.betting_forecast: 11/4 Armstrong, 4/1 Chapman's Peak, 9/2 Crafty Blue, 15/2 Tewkesbury,  Silver State, 11/1 Glasgow Kiss, 14/1 Trio,  Foothold, 20/1 Halla Bil Zain,  Grand Pier,  Atalanta Mist

racecards.race_name: Try Unibet's New Racing Betbuilder Handicap (Div I)

runners.breeder: Lynn Lodge Stud & Pier House Stud
runners.comment: Won at Wolverhampton in December but she's been disappointing since and is now 1-24
runners.spotlight: Off the mark when awarded a race at Wolverhampton (9.4f, Tapeta) in December but she's finished a well-held eighth there in both subsequent runs; overall record is now 1-24 and others are more convincing.

runners.comment: Turf winner who has a record of 3143231 on AW for current yard; key player
runners.spotlight: Won on turf in Ireland last summer and he has form figures of 3143231 on AW since joining his current yard; up another 4lb but he knuckled down well at Wolverhampton last time and he remains well handicapped on his best form; key player in his bid for a double.

runners.comment: Ran well at Wolverhampton last month and he's in the mix back on turf
runners.spotlight: His last win was in September 2024 but that was off 19lb higher at Chester, and he ran well to finish third at Wolverhampton (8.6f) last month; still lightly raced on turf and has possibilities if he handles the conditions back in this sphere (best form has been on soft ground).

runners.comment: Triple C&D winner who reappeared with a good second on AW last month; respected
runners.spotlight: Triple C&D winner (good/firm) who returned after six months off with a front-running second on AW at Lingfield (1m) last month; on unchanged mark and he's an interesting contender back at this track.

runners.comment: C&D winner but he doesn't have a great record when fresh and this is competitive
runners.spotlight: Completed a double off 2lb higher over C&D (firm) last May but he's not hit the same level in five runs since; has bit to prove after 171 days off and he doesn't have a great record when fresh; visor is removed and cheekpieces are reapplied.

runners.comment: Won at Wolverhampton last month but he's been disappointing in both subsequent runs
runners.spotlight: Readily saw off eight rivals at Wolverhampton (8.6f) last month but he's been disappointing in both subsequent runs; has something to prove again and he has form figures of 5097 at Bath.

runners.comment: Record of 1-27 but her win came over C&D and she ran respectably here two weeks ago
runners.spotlight: Record of 1-27 but her win came over C&D (firm) last summer and she returned from a break with a fair fifth (1m, good) here two weeks ago; has claims if she can build on that and she won't mind what the weather does.

runners.owner: Mrs Wendy Jarrett & J S Moore
runners.comment: Triple C&D winner and he needs watching in market after 169 days off
runners.spotlight: Eight-time turf winner including three over C&D (good to firm/firm); well handicapped on his best form in 2025 but he's not easy to predict and he ended last season on a low note; market should guide after 169 days off.

stable_tour.quote: I've got two lovely old campaigners who are half-brothers - Fact Or Fable and Uther Pendragon. Between the two of them, they've won just short of £200,000 in prize-money. They always turn up and probably on the days you'd don't expect them to win, they do. They're characters in the yard and keep everybody on their toes who rides them. They're owned by the same people - Wendy and Stuart Jarrett - who get so much fun out of it. It's what the game's about. Wendy and Stuart have point-to-pointers as well and they absolutely love their racing. They come from the Bath area and that's why, when you see them, they'll always turn up at Bath and Chepstow. They're the sort of owners racing needs, who are in it just for the love of the sport. 04-07-24

runners.comment: Plenty of decent efforts last year but his last win was in 2023; others preferred
runners.spotlight: Some fair efforts on AW during the winter and he hit the frame plenty of times on turf last year; hard to rule out a good run after a short break but he's not won since 2023 and others are preferred.

quotes.race: Rotherby Handicap
quotes.quote: Everything went wrong for Eye Of The Water at Wolverhampton last time but, although he's won at that track, he's a much better horse on soft ground. That's the key to him - Ron Harris, trainer.

quotes.race: Molson Coors Handicap
quotes.quote: Last time Eye Of The Water ran on soft ground at Ffos Las he won. Conditions were slightly heavier today and he relished them. He was able to get a smart break and he never saw another horse after that - David Probert, jockey.

racecards.verdict: Top of the list is GALAXY WONDER who won on turf last summer and has form figures of 3143231 on AW since joining his current yard.

runners.comment: 5yo who has not progressed and has form figures of 839837 in handicaps; down the list

stable_tour.quote: He's run only once but that was a very pleasing debut at Salisbury last July when he won by a length and three-quarters. He had a hold-up after that but he's training nicely and I'm looking forward to getting him back on the track. 17-04-25

prev_owners.owner: Exors Of The Late S F Hui

runners.comment: Showed signs of a revival at Wolverhampton and has claims if he can build on that

quotes.race: PricedUp.Bet Grassroots Series Middle Distance Final Handicap (GBBPlus Race)
quotes.quote: Annexation won nicely at Bath on Tuesday and got a bit of confidence, so it's a great performance from him today. It's a great prize and a good bit of placing! He's come without a penalty, unfortunately the boy who won on him the other day (Matthew Lloyd Slater) couldn't do the weight so Jack rode him - Tony Carroll, trainer.

quotes.race: Crowne Plaza Hotel Dundalk Race & Stay Handicap
quotes.quote: Annexation missed the beat a bit and it was ideal as I had something to aim at the whole way. I think this is his ideal trip and he could win another one up here - Chris Hayes, rider

stable_tour.quote: He was really good at Navan in his maiden hurdle and we were aiming for the novice hurdle at Tipperary but he wasn't right. He seems in good form again and we might aim him at the For Auction Novice Hurdle at Navan. He handled soft ground on the Flat, although whether he'll be as effective on it over hurdles we'll see. We'll feel our way with him in the autumn and if he handles soft ground we can plot our way through the winter with him. 09-11-20

runners.comment: Back on last winning mark but he needs a major revival back on turf; cheekpieces removed
runners.spotlight: Won four Class 6 handicaps (7f-1m) in 2025, including on good to firm and heavy ground; back on last winning mark but he's been out of sorts in last four runs and needs a major revival back on turf; cheekpieces removed.

quotes.race: 'Phil Saunders Miracle 70th' Handicap (Chepstow Mile Series Qualifier)
quotes.quote: Arjad has always been a bit too clever. We've dropped him in the last couple of times and he seems to really enjoy it. Before that we had him a bit handier, but he was a bit resentful - Rod Millman, trainer, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

stable_tour.quote: He's come back to form with a ­vengeance with two wins and two seconds in his last four runs. All of them have been at ­Chepstow and we've held him up, running him a bit ­differently. The first time he ran well over 7f, ­winning on his side, but the ­winner came and did him late on the ­opposite side of the track. We always thought he was a bit ­clever, but then he won his next two over a mile and seems to have turned a ­corner. On ­Monday he was ­second again in the £35,000 ­final of the ­Chepstow Mile Series. If he's in the mood, he's still ­potentially well ­handicapped. 27-08-25

runners.comment: Six-race maiden who has struggled in his three handicaps; lots to prove with visor added
runners.spotlight: Went close in a Wolverhampton maiden (7f, AW) in December 2024 but he's struggled since including in three handicaps this winter; still lightly raced but he has plenty to prove on turf debut; visor added.

runners.comment: In good form on AW for new yard and she's respected back on turf
runners.spotlight: Record of 533313 for new stable and that latest third was a creditable effort from off the pace at Wolverhampton (8.6f) last month; on same mark here and she's a big player if she can continue the good work back on turf.

runners.spotlight: 4yo filly who was beaten 5l or more in seven runs (1m-1m2f) for Stuart Kittow last season; returns for new trainer after 163 days off and she needs improvement back on turf.

runners.comment: Both wins were in 2024 and was well held on reappearance over C&D 12 days ago

runners.breeder: Moyns Park Estate And Stud Ltd

stable_tour.quote: He was second on his debut at Leicester in a three-horse race, but that doesn't tell the story. He was very slowly away and lost several lengths yet still managed to run on and get second once the penny dropped. I am not saying he would have beaten the winner but he would have been much closer. 10-05-23

runners.comment: Dual turf winner who is on a dangerous mark back in this sphere; needs watching market

quotes.race: Jack Challis Turns 12 Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: I think Stinginhisstep will be a nice horse, it might take another 12 months. He's not easy, but we've got him settled at home and he's better on the racecourse - Sue Gardner, trainer, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

quotes.race: Amber Stevens Novices' Limited Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: What impressed me was how well Springinhisstep stayed, he would be better over a further trip. He's progressive so we hope there's plenty more to come from him. We could tell this week he'd come on from his last race so we knew we had a good chance today. Sean [Houlihan, jockey] said he can't wait to get him over fences - Sue Gardner, trainer.

runners.comment: Multiple winner across both codes; ground suits; 6lb higher than last win; competitive.
runners.spotlight: Multiple Flat winner at up to 1m6f and dual hurdles winner at up to 2m3f; goes well on a sound surface; 6lb higher than when scoring at Taunton on his penultimate start; beaten more than 9l when unpenalised at Plumpton latest, but should be competitive.

quotes.race: Betting.Bet Free Horse Racing Tips Handicap (Bath Summer Stayers' Series Qualifier)
quotes.quote: Joe (Tickle) said Taritino needs a bit of daylight and if he doesn't jump he can be tricky but he did jump. To be fair he was very free, I managed to get two breathers into him but when the other horse came alongside he lit me up again. It was a good effort considering. He'll probably get 2m - Hollie Doyle, jockey, speaking to Sky Racing.

runners.comment: 2m hurdle winner (soft); held when up 7lb latest; drops 1lb; back up in trip; more needed.
runners.spotlight: Made all for a 2m hurdle win (soft) under Tom Broughton at Southwell on his penultimate start; up 7lb when weakening out of it at Chepstow (2m, good to soft; first-time cheekpieces); drops 1lb; goes back up in trip with more needed.

runners.owner: Mrs D Robinson Mrs & Mrs Livesey-Van Dorst
runners.comment: 2m3f chase winner here; well beaten over fences recently; bit to prove back hurdling.
runners.spotlight: 2m3f chase winner here (good) 12 months ago; 0-6 over hurdles; well beaten over fences on his last four starts; bit to prove back hurdling.

runners.comment: Well beaten all three starts; much more needed even from this mark on handicap debut.
runners.spotlight: Triple-figure odds and well beaten in all three qualifying starts; much more needed even from this lowly mark on her handicap debut.

runners.spotlight: Two-time winner over hurdles on good to soft, at around 2m (acts on a sound surface); stays 2m5f; some way below his best since last spring; well treated on form of almost a year ago if bouncing back but has that to prove.

stable_tour.quote: He's new to me this season and I was worried before his first run on the Flat because he'd shown me nothing in his work but he ran a perfectly sound race and has another run at Nottingham on Wednesday. He will return to hurdling later this season and he showed some decent form last season. 07-11-24

runners.comment: C&D winner who scored over 3m (good) latest; up 6lb but looks a leading player.
runners.spotlight: C&D winner last November (good to soft; held up), when 15lb lower; also held up when showing marginal improvement to score at Wincanton (3m, good) latest; up another 6lb but looks a leading player.

runners.comment: 0-14 and looks in need of further favours from the handicapper to break his duck.
runners.spotlight: 0-14 under rules; sliding in the weights in four starts for this trainer and those efforts suggest he'll need a further favour or two from the handicapper to break his duck.

runners.comment: Inconsistent; better efforts would give him an each-way chance, if getting this trip.
runners.spotlight: 0-11 (placed twice at Taunton over 2m3f); inconsistent but better efforts would give him an each-way chance from this mark, if seeing out this longer trip.

runners.comment: C&D winner (good to firm); held on last two starts; more needed but not written off.

runners.comment: 2m4f hurdle and 2m7f chase winner; competitive mark if shrugging off below-par C&D effort.
runners.spotlight: 2m4f hurdle and 2m7f chase winner (both good to soft); versatile regarding going but yet to race on good to firm; on a competitive mark if he can shrug off a lesser effort over C&D latest.

quotes.race: Happy Birthday Lyndsey Lane From Brunel Novices' Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: I didn't really want to make the running. Watchoutitscookie has a tendency to go to his right, but as long as you don't fight him, he's pretty straightforward that way. So I made the running on him, he's jumped well, and he's done it well - Lorcan Murtagh, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

quotes.race: Newt In Somerset Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: Watchoutitscookie has been quite difficult. He's been keen and the hood has helped. It was a good run last time and he was the one today. I think he wants a bit of cut in the ground and he's in at Exeter tomorrow, but we'll see how he is in the morning. I think he'll build on this because he has been difficult and keen. With horses like that, why fight them? He's taught himself to settle if you like - Nigel Hawke, trainer.

runners.owner: The Cheltenham & South West Racing Club
runners.comment: C&D winner; better over hurdles but was unable to take advantage over C&D latest.
runners.spotlight: C&D (good to soft) and 3m chase winner (good) who is back on that last winning chase mark; has been better in this discipline and is on a handy mark but was unable to take advantage over C&D latest.

quotes.race: Visit racingtv.com Novices' Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: Moonlight Artist has gone off favourite or a short price a few times and I've always wondered why but he got it together today. This should do his confidence the world of good and hopefully there should be another race in him. Brendan Powell, rider.

stable_tour.quote: He was in training all of last season and ready to run but we didn't want to risk him on the ground. He'll go novice hurdling in the middle of November but works nicely. He seems like a nice horse. 31-10-22

runners.comment: 2m7f hurdle winner; on a lengthy losing run and has plenty to prove from 4lb wrong.

runners.spotlight: Rattled off a hat-trick at Ludlow (2m) in February but he beat only one off a 7lb higher mark in 2m1f Newcastle handicap six days ago; could bounce back off a 2lb lower mark.

quotes.race: JTC Pizzalicious Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Thank You Blue jumped really well. He'll probably be better over a little bit further, I was just forcing him for the last half a mile. He was good over the last two and galloped to the line - Sean Quinlan, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

stable_tour.quote: Like Constitution Hill he's a son of Blue Bresil and it's incredible how jumping issues came to the fore with this guy - not over hurdles but over fences. He fell twice and was pulled up three times over fences but he's done very well this season back over hurdles, winning his last three. He'll run again under a penalty this week - he has two entries at Ayr on Friday, one over fences and one over hurdles. 04-03-26

runners.comment: Not disgraced after five months off when sixth in handicap here 26 days ago; considered
runners.spotlight: Bagged a pair of handicaps (around 2m4f) at Chepstow and Warwick before Christmas and wasn't disgraced after five months off when sixth in 2m7f handicap here 26 days ago; considered.

runners.comment: Won here in March; just fourth of five at Wincanton since so more needed going h'capping
runners.spotlight: Debut bumper winner who opened his account in this sphere in 2m maiden here in March; failed to build on it when fourth of five in 2m5f Wincanton novice since though so more is required now going handicapping.

runners.spotlight: A fair 2m5f hurdles winner at his best but he's yet to fire for his current yard, blinkered when unseated rider four out in 2m3f Fontwell handicap nine days ago; others appeal more.

I had a target two out when I chased the leader and hit the front at the right time as he may have pricked his ears if he was in front too long. The ground on the stands rail was less churned up and he enjoyed it - Gavin Sheehan, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: He's one of those consistent handicappers who always wins his races. It didn't quite happen for him over fences last year, but he appreciated going back over hurdles when a good second at Bangor. 05-11-25
